requirements.statement: The notification type question offers radio options in this order, with no hint text and none pre-selected on a new start: Live animals; Germinal products (semen, ova, embryos); Plants for planting; Potatoes (seed and ware); Wood products. Live animals continues to the animals frontend's live-animals start, which creates the GBN-AG draft with the live-animals category and lands on its origin page. Germinal products continues to the start of the germinal products set, the live-animals set's sibling in the animals frontend, which creates its own GBN-AG draft with the germinal products category and lands on that set's origin page; this option may land before the germinal products set itself is built. Plants for planting, Potatoes (seed and ware) and Wood products continue to the start of the high-risk plants journey in trade-imports-plants-frontend, which creates a plants draft and lands on plants' own first page.
requirements.why: The target design's options and order, with each type sent to the real service or set that takes it: the real services split journeys by type, each creating its own draft and reference (c-007). The 9 October ruling offers Germinal products second and makes it start the germinal products set, each set passing its category when it creates the draft, and lets the link land ahead of the set. The templates ruling gives plants the same entry from the INS type question.

requirements.statement: The reference data service serves GET /countries: a JSON array of code (MDM effectiveAlpha2), name (effectiveAlias) and subDivisions (code and name), sorted by name, with the United Kingdom always removed and, when blocks is given, only countries whose matching MDM block has includeCountry true.
requirements.why: The country list the origin page offers comes from this endpoint; it already does what the journey needs, and the list content stays MDM's.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-referencedata-p1-073 proves GET /countries?blocks=GBNAG_SPS_EX returns sorted countries with subdivisions and no UK.

requirements.statement: The reference data service reads countries from MDM's geography list for the GBNAG system, with the platform subscription key and a client-credentials bearer token reused until it expires.
requirements.why: The MDM integration behind the country list already exists.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-referencedata-p1-068 proves the GBNAG system and blocks value are passed to MDM.

requirements.statement: The reference data service caches MDM countries per blocks value (and ports) in memory for 60 minutes by default, at most 20 entries, and never caches an empty result.
requirements.why: Existing behaviour that limits calls to MDM.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-referencedata-p1-075 and repo-referencedata-p1-076 prove the countries cache, its per-blocks keys and expiry.

requirements.statement: The reference data service answers an empty MDM countries result with an empty list, and any unexpected failure (including a failed MDM call) with a 500 RFC 7807 problem body carrying the trace id.
requirements.why: Existing error behaviour behind the country list.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-referencedata-p1-071 and repo-referencedata-p1-081 prove the empty list and the problem bodies.

requirements.statement: The reference data service stays the shared home for MDM-sourced reference domains (ADR 0002), serving countries and ports of entry on port 8086 with per-endpoint response-time and external-call metrics.
requirements.why: Existing ruling and operation of the service; nothing in Design Release 2.1 changes it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-referencedata-p1-083 and repo-referencedata-p1-084 record ADR 0002 with countries a managed MDM domain.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: adding commodity, species, commodity identifier, transporter, document type or certification purpose lists to the reference data service, or documenting its endpoints in its README.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks for no change to where those lists are served, and nothing in this area needs them in the reference data service.

requirements.statement: The commodity page has the browser title 'What are you importing? - Import notification service - GOV.UK', the caption 'About the consignment' above the heading 'What are you importing?', the Draft tag and notification reference above the caption, and a search field labelled 'Search for a commodity'.
requirements.why: The page's frame already matches Design Release 2.1 and must stay as it is while the rest of the page changes.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p8-003, -p8-004, -p8-005, -p8-006 and -p8-008 show the same title, caption, heading, Draft strip and label today.

requirements.statement: The commodity page's inset text reads 'You must submit a separate notification for every single ITAHC. You must also submit a notification for goods that do not need an ITAHC.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 words the one-notification-per-certificate rule in terms of the ITAHC, the certificate traders know.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the inset reads 'A separate notification is required for each health certificate. Consignments that do not require a health certificate must still be notified.' (trace-animals-fit-p8-007).

requirements.statement: On a live-animals notification the commodity search hint reads 'You can search by common name (for example, cattle), commodity code (0102), or Latin name (Bos taurus).', with no 'Enter at least 3 characters.' sentence.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording wins by default; DR1 left the hint wording unruled, and the reason the frontend departed from it (no common names in the data) no longer holds, since 'cattle' now finds cattle species. Ruling 2026-10-09 afternoon lets the commodity pages' wording go ahead on today's data. The germinal set's own hint ('You can search for semen, ova or embryos, ...', prototype-dr2-1-source-p2-077) is the germinal-products area's requirement; it is cited here only to show the live-animals hint is the live set's alone.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the hint reads 'You can search by commodity name (for example, Cow), commodity code (0102), or species name (Bos taurus). Enter at least 3 characters.' (trace-animals-fit-p8-009); the Welsh mirrors it.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, the 'What are you importing?' page keeps the live-animals title, caption, heading, ITAHC inset, label, buttons, Cancel link and back link (to the origin page), and its search hint reads 'You can search for semen, ova or embryos, or by common name (for example, cattle), Latin name (Bos taurus) or commodity code (05119985).'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 tells a trader importing germinal products what they can search for, and changes nothing else on the page. The 9 October afternoon ruling lets the germinal set's copy of today's commodity page, with this hint, go ahead on today's commodity data; no trace shows a germinal error state on this page, so its errors are the live-animal page's.
requirements.deltaNote: The real animals frontend has no germinal products set today.

requirements.statement: A closed 'Help with commodity codes' details component below the search explains 'Commodity codes are internationally recognised reference numbers.' and 'A commodity code describes a specific product when importing or exporting goods.', and links to the Trade Tariff tool at https://www.gov.uk/trade-tariff in a new tab.
requirements.why: Traders who do not know their commodity code need a way to look it up.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p8-012 to -p8-016 show the same details summary, both paragraphs and the new-tab Trade Tariff link today.

requirements.statement: In the commodity code help, '(opens in a new tab)' sits on its own line after the 'Trade Tariff tool' link, as Design Release 2.1 lays it out, and stays part of the link's accessible text.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 breaks the line before '(opens in a new tab)'; keeping the words inside the link keeps the link purpose announced, as the page's accessibility check requires.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the link text 'Trade Tariff tool (opens in a new tab)' runs on one line with the sentence (trace-animals-fit-p8-015).

requirements.statement: The germinal products set's commodity search offers only germinal-product commodities, and the live-animals set's catalogue no longer holds the 12 germinal lines it holds today, so neither set offers the other's commodities.
requirements.why: Each set holds one category, so a consignment mixing live animals and germinal products is never written; each set's catalogue holds only its own commodities. Splitting today's lines between the sets is set architecture, not list content, so it goes ahead without waiting on MDM.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the live-animals commodity catalogue holds 12 germinal lines (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-026) and there is no germinal set; the germinal lines move out of live animals into the germinal set's own catalogue.

requirements.statement: Once commodities come from MDM, the germinal products catalogue holds the V4 page's 12 germinal commodities, with embryos and ova as separate items: Cattle, Goat, Horse, Pig and Sheep each as '<Animal>, Embryos' and '<Animal>, Ova' (05119985); and '<Animal>, Semen' for Cattle (05111000), Cat, Dog (V4's 'Semen - Dog or Cat'), Goat, Horse, Pig, Rabbit/Rodent and Sheep (05119985): 18 items, sorted by name, codes shown with their leading zero. Each item offers the species Design Release 2.1 lists under that animal (Cattle: Bison bison, Bos taurus and Bubalus bubalis, plus Bovidae for semen; Horse: Equus asinus and Equus caballus; Goat: Capra hircus; Pig: Sus scrofa domesticus; Sheep: Ovis aries; Cat: Felis catus; Dog: Canis familiaris; Rabbit/Rodent semen: one row labelled Rabbit/Rodent). There are no poultry, fish or bee germinal products and no Cat or Dog embryos or ova.
requirements.why: A germinal products notification needs germinal commodities to choose from. V4 sets which germinal commodities the data applies to; the GBN-AG schema has separate EMBRYO and OVA type codes, so embryos and ova are separate items; Design Release 2.1 gives the species and the names. Its Cat and Dog embryos and ova are mock data the 9 October ruling does not copy, and V4 gives them no fields (c-230). The 9 October afternoon ruling makes this 18-item catalogue wait on MDM (c-282).
requirements.blockedBy: Commodities come from MDM (ruling 9 October afternoon, point 2), and the germinal commodity catalogue and search are re-distilled from that list; until then the germinal set offers today's 12 germinal lines (req-1927).

requirements.statement: Each reason carries its hint: Internal market 'For imports of animals intended for sale or use in Great Britain (England, Scotland or Wales).'; Transhipment or onward travel 'For animals intended for direct travel to a third country, that will stay only within the same port or airport in Great Britain while moving to another means of transport.'; Transit 'For animals moving through Great Britain for direct travel to a third country, that will enter Great Britain at one port or airport and leave from a different one within England, Scotland or Wales.'; Re-entry 'For animals authorised for re-entry, or rejected exports re-entering Great Britain.'; Temporary admission horses 'For horses authorised for temporary entry.'

requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p7-059 and trace-animals-fit-p12-029 show the 'Error: ' prefix and HTTP 400 today.

requirements.statement: When a saved destination country, port of exit or certification purpose is no longer in the reference list, reopening the page says so ('The saved destination country is no longer available. Select a country from the list.', 'The saved port of exit is no longer available. Select a port from the list.', 'The certification purpose you chose is no longer offered. Select a purpose from the list.') and blanks it in every reveal.
requirements.why: A saved answer going stale against reference data is a persistence constraint the prototype cannot express, so the real service keeps handling it.

requirements.statement: Both pages end with a 'Save and continue' button, a secondary 'Save and return to overview' button and a 'Cancel and return to overview' link to the notification hub.

requirements.statement: 'Save and return to overview' on the main import reason page saves without the required checks and goes to the hub: it saves the chosen reason, keeps only the follow-up answers that belong to it (a missing follow-up is saved as empty) and clears the other reasons' answers; with no reason chosen it changes nothing already saved. An exit date that is not a real calendar date is still refused with 'Enter a real date', as on Save and continue. When amending, the 'Save and return' (review) action does the same and goes to the review page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 defines the soft save this way and the prototype wins by default, except that c-211 settles that an answer failing its own format rule, such as an impossible date, is refused rather than silently dropped: the real service cannot store a value that does not fit its field.
requirements.deltaNote: No today source in this area shows what 'Save and return to overview' does on this page (trace-animals-fit-p7-079); the builder reads the shared save actions and changes only what differs.

requirements.statement: When the main import reason page is opened while editing a template from its review, the Back link goes to that template's review, and saving saves the template and returns to its review with a '<title> has been updated' message. Template mode walks this same page, never a copy of it, so later changes to the page carry into template mode; it applies to the animals sets only.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets a template be edited page by page from its review; the templates ruling makes template mode another way through the same journey pages, with Back links that follow the context the page was opened in, and builds it on the pages as they stand. The templates area owns the template itself.
requirements.deltaNote: No today source in this area shows template editing reaching this page.

requirements.statement: The main import reason task counts as complete once a reason allowed for the notification is saved with valid follow-ups (Internal market an allowed purpose; Transhipment a listed country; Transit a listed port and country; Temporary admission horses a real exit date and listed port; Re-entry nothing more), whether or not Additional details is answered; with no reason saved it is not complete.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 judges the reason section on its own answers and has Additional details as a separate task.
requirements.deltaNote: On latest main the 'Main reason for import' row completes only once the Additional details page after it is saved too (trace-e2e-p4-112, trace-e2e-p4-116); the fit traces at an older commit showed it complete on the reason alone (trace-animals-fit-p7-054).

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, an animal counts as entered once at least one identifier its species asks for has a value: it is saved, listed in the saved-animals table and the panel moves on to the next animal, with the other identifiers left blank.

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, pressing a species panel's 'Save and add another' or 'Save and finish' with every identifier of the current animal blank saves nothing and shows 'Enter at least one identifier for this animal' in the error summary and inline, linked to that panel's first identifier field. The check is made per panel, so an empty panel is refused even when another species' form holds data. A partly filled animal saves with no error. The page's 'Save and continue' and 'Save and return to overview' never block on missing identifiers: an empty form saves no record and the trader moves on, and the page shows no message about the submit rule.
requirements.why: One identifier is enough (9 October ruling), so DR1's per-identifier errors, which it asked for only if every identifier were ruled required, are not built. A status the service cannot read shows a grey 'Unknown' tag.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 simulates a scan that always passes, so it has no failure state. A real scan can find a virus: a real constraint the prototype cannot express, so the real failure handling stays.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-075 and trace-e2e-p12-037 show the Virus found state and its error today.

requirements.statement: While a document is scanning, the page updates its status without the trader acting: with JavaScript it polls a JSON status endpoint every 3 seconds up to 10 times, updates settled rows in place, announces 'Document scan complete: the file is safe to use' or 'Document scan failed: a virus was found. Remove the file and try again.' in a polite live region, and redraws from the server once every scan settles; without JavaScript a 'Refresh virus scan status' link re-reads the status; after 10 attempts the hint 'Still checking some documents. Refresh again in a moment.' shows.
requirements.why: A real scan takes time; the trader needs to see it finish. Design Release 2.1 fakes this with a timed call, which the real scan replaces. The polling is the real service's own enhancement, not script written to copy the prototype, and the refresh link means nothing the trader needs is shown only by script, as Sam's 9 October afternoon ruling requires.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-097 to repo-frontend-p8-101 and trace-e2e-p12-048 show polling, announcements and the no-JavaScript refresh link today.

requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 never stores a file, so it cannot show one; storing and serving the real file is a persistence constraint the prototype cannot express, and the trader needs to check what they attached.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-064 and trace-e2e-p12-052 offer and serve View file for clean documents today.

Sam's 9 October ruling confirms a page opened from its overview task returns to the overview on Save and continue (claim 39), without a ?from=hub marker (c-237).

The return context is carried by the service's own mechanisms (the live flow's fallback to the overview, and the existing ?change=1 for review); no ?from=hub or ?from=review marker and no hidden 'from' field is added.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 returns the trader to where they started however often the page reloads, and that is the behaviour kept. How the context travels is architecture: Sam's 9 October ruling says no ?from=hub marker is added and only the live flow's fallback changes (claim 39), and query parameter and form field names are the service's (claim 17).

requirements.statement: While a trader is creating a template, Upload documents is not offered: the one journey's template mode skips the page and its overview has no Documents task to follow. requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps documents out of templates, because a document belongs to one consignment, and Sam's 9 October ruling confirms a template never offers documents and that the prototype's template URL guards are not required (c-238). His templates ruling makes template mode a way of walking the same pages, never copied or forked, and animals only; it says nothing to bring documents into a template, so the earlier, specific exclusion stands and is built inside that one journey.

requirements.statement: The overview's 'Upload documents' link can be followed as soon as the origin of the import is answered, before the commodity or any later section is complete.

requirements.statement: The overview has a section '4. Documents' with one task, 'Upload documents', linking to the page; it shows 'To do' while no document has been added and 'Complete' once documents are saved.

requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p12-001, trace-e2e-p12-002 and trace-animals-fit-p22-066 show the task, To do and Complete today.

requirements.statement: Each document is saved to the notification as soon as it is added, as its own record in the backend's accompanying_documents collection keyed by the notification reference, with its type code, reference, date of issue as a YYYY-MM-DD date, a UUID upload id, scan status and files; it is still listed on a fresh load, and a retried save or removal does not add or remove it twice.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps documents in the session and only saves the draft on some buttons. Storing them durably is a persistence constraint the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-014, repo-tests-p3-048 and repo-tests-p3-056 show each document stored and still listed after a reload today.

requirements.statement: The file goes from the browser to the frontend, which sends it through the backend to cdp-uploader for virus scanning and storage in the documents S3 bucket; cdp-uploader reports the result to the backend's scan-result callback, matched by correlation id, and a document becomes COMPLETE only when no file was rejected (fail closed). A failure to reach or use the uploader shows 'The file could not be uploaded. Try again.'. In CDP the scan is the real cdp-uploader; on the local stack it is the stack's cdp-uploader container with a mock scan.
requirements.why: This is the real upload handshake behind the page; Design Release 2.1 sends only the filename and cannot express it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-003, repo-backend-p4-018 and repo-backend-p4-063 show the proxied cdp-uploader flow working end to end today.

requirements.statement: Documents can be added and removed whatever the notification's status, are deleted with their notification, and only documents that scanned clean are referenced in the events the backend publishes.
requirements.why: These are the cross-service rules around the document record; the design does not contradict them, and amending a notification reaches the page in DR2.1 too.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-078, repo-backend-p4-079 and repo-backend-p4-080 hold these rules today.

requirements.statement: The documents page stays safe and recoverable: text the trader typed is HTML-escaped in table cells; a failed delete of an upload leaves the document in place; a saved document whose type the service no longer lists raises 'One or more of your saved documents are no longer valid. Review the list before you continue.'.
requirements.why: Real-service safeguards with no design counterpart; DR2.1 does not contradict them.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-063, repo-frontend-p8-067 and repo-frontend-p8-084 hold these safeguards today.

requirements.statement: The documents page has no serious or critical axe violations (WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 AA) when empty, in its error state, with the date picker open, with the guidance expanded, with a file chosen and with a saved scanned document.

requirements.statement: Backend document-endpoint defects: initiating or listing uploads never checks the notification exists or its reference format; the endpoints have no per-user or per-organisation scoping; the scan callback is unauthenticated; deleting a document leaves its file in S3; a download that fails mid-stream returns a truncated 200; the list has no defined order; and the API description of the scan callback omits its 400 and 404.
requirements.why: Real problems in the backend that Design Release 2.1 says nothing about and this programme does not fix; they go to the report.

requirements.statement: Each picker row ends with a 'View' link that opens that address in the INS address book, carrying a return path that brings the trader back to the same picker. This is the animals pickers' change only: the high-risk plants frontend is not wired to the INS address book, so its pickers keep their 'View details' disclosure.

requirements.statement: Reopening a picker for a party that already has an address picked from the book pre-selects that address's radio; a copy that was edited, or whose record has gone from the book, opens with nothing selected. The high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers already pre-select the saved address, and a saved reference whose record has gone opens with nothing selected.
requirements.why: The prototype pre-selects the current choice, and the real picker already does.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-073 and trace-animals-fit-p14-070 show the saved address pre-selected today.

requirements.statement: Pressing 'Save and continue' on a party picker with no address chosen shows no error and leaves the party as it was, empty or holding its earlier address. An animals party picker returns to the roles and addresses page; the high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers move on as their save does, to the next page of the journey.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader leave a picker without choosing; completeness is checked by the task status and the review, not by the picker. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm gives plants' consignor and place of destination pickers the same lenient blank save in the same increment (inc-086); plants' task status still shows the party as not done.
requirements.deltaNote: Today saving with nothing chosen keeps an address already held (repo-frontend-p9-079), but with none held it re-renders the picker with status 400 and 'Select a <party> from the list' (repo-frontend-p9-080, trace-animals-fit-p14-050 to -054). Plants re-shows the page with 'Select a place of destination from the list' or 'Select a consignor from the list' and status 400 when nothing is chosen (repo-plantsfrontend-p6-032, repo-plantsfrontend-p6-058, repo-plantsfrontend-p6-075, repo-plantsfrontend-p6-086).

requirements.statement: Saving a picker with an address that is not in the organisation's book, or has been deleted since the page loaded, saves nothing and re-renders the picker with status 400, an error summary 'There is a problem' and the party's error: 'Select a place of origin from the list', 'Select a consignor from the list', 'Select a consignee from the list', 'Select an importer from the list' or 'Select a place of destination from the list' (and their Welsh), the summary link going to the first address radio, or to the search box when there are no rows. The high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers keep the same refusal of an id the address book does not hold, with 'Select a consignor from the list' or 'Select a place of destination from the list', the message shown above the results table with a visually hidden 'Error:' prefix, and the summary link to the first row's radio or, with no rows, the search box.
requirements.why: A real constraint the prototype cannot express: the notification must never hold a party copied from a record the organisation does not have, so today's refusal stays for that case.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-081 shows an id not in the organisation's book, or soft-deleted, refused with the party error today. repo-plantsfrontend-p6-088, repo-plantsfrontend-p6-019 and repo-plantsfrontend-p6-031 show plants refusing such an id the same way today.

requirements.statement: Outside an amendment, each of the five party pickers (place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer, place of destination) and the CPH number page end with a single primary 'Save and continue' button, with no 'Save and return to hub' button and no cancel link. While amending, their endings are req-1624's.
requirements.why: DR1 ruled this same difference (rule (b)): only pages the overview links to end with the three return controls, and a page reached from another page ends with the primary button alone; the pickers are reached from the roles and addresses page.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-078, trace-e2e-p9-045 and trace-animals-fit-p15-030 show the pickers ending with 'Save and continue' alone today, and document-dr1-parity-notes-p1-057 records the CPH number page built the same way under DR1 rule (b). The permanent address page follows the same rule (req-748).

requirements.statement: Choosing an address on a picker and pressing 'Save and continue' saves on the notification a copy of that record (the record it came from, name, phone, email and address) and returns to the roles and addresses page, or to check your answers under change context. The roles and addresses page names each party from that copy, never from the address book, including after submission. This copy is the animals frontend's: the high-risk plants frontend keeps saving a reference to the record instead.
requirements.why: The prototype and the real service both save the chosen address against the party and return to the page; the copy keeps the notification stable when the book changes.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-085, repo-frontend-p9-086 and trace-e2e-p9-044 show the copy saved and the redirect to the roles and addresses page today.

requirements.statement: If saving a picked address fails with a recoverable backend error, the picker re-renders with status 500, the recoverable-error message and the choice still selected. The high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers do the same, keeping the chosen address and search term.
requirements.why: A real persistence constraint the prototype cannot express: the trader must not lose their choice when the save fails.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-088 shows this behaviour today.

requirements.statement: Each party picker, on both animals sets and on the high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers, offers only the organisation's addresses whose roles include that party's role: place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer or place of destination.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 filters each picker to its role, so a trader is not offered a GB importer as a place of origin; DR1 found the unfiltered list a live defect on all the pickers, and ruling sam-2026-10-09 keeps address roles because DR1 asked for role-filtered pickers. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm builds the role-filtered pickers now (inc-087) and gives plants the same change in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today all five pickers search one undifferentiated book with no address type (repo-frontend-p9-047), so every role offers the same addresses (trace-animals-fit-p14-045). Plants' pickers search the organisation's whole book by search term alone (repo-plantsfrontend-p6-006).

requirements.statement: The consignor picker offers addresses saved for the consignor role, including any saved as an exporter; there is no separate exporter party. How the address book records those roles is the address book's design.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's consignor section covers the exporter too, and accepts addresses saved as either. Ruling sam-2026-10-09 leaves the field shape of address roles to the address book service, so the prototype's type values are not copied.

requirements.statement: An address saved with several roles appears on the picker of every party whose role it carries.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets one saved address be reused across parties, such as the same company as consignee and importer.

requirements.statement: The address book (trade-imports-address-book) holds one or more roles on each address record and lets a frontend list an organisation's addresses for one role, unpaginated and still excluding deleted records; the animals frontend and the high-risk plants frontend each ask for their picker's role. The record's field shape for roles is the address book service's own design, not the prototype's.
requirements.why: DR1 found role filtering needs a typed address record, which no frontend can fake; the address book is one of this programme's repos, so the record shape and the role-aware list are built here. Ruling sam-2026-10-09 keeps address roles (inc-087) and leaves their field shape to the address book. Collecting the roles when an address is saved is the address-book and party-address-add-and-edit areas' work.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the address-book record carries no type and its list call takes only a page and a search text (repo-frontend-p9-047, repo-frontend-p9-159). Plants' address-book service reads the organisation's whole book a page at a time by search term alone, for every picker (repo-plantsfrontend-p6-006).

requirements.statement: An address-book record that has no role yet (every record saved before roles exist) is offered on every party picker, in the animals frontend and in the high-risk plants frontend, until it is given a role, in the compose stack and in CDP alike.
requirements.why: Records saved before roles existed are a persistence constraint the prototype cannot express, and DR1's inc-048 judgement rules out filtering them on a guess, which would hide addresses the trader legitimately wants (c-101).

requirements.statement: In stub mode, each canned address-book record carries one or more roles, in the animals frontend's stub and in the high-risk plants frontend's stub book, so the stub-mode pickers filter by role as the real ones do.
requirements.why: The stub mirrors the tests repo's address-book fixture record for record and is what local development and the frontend suite run against; without roles it cannot show role filtering.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the stub is 13 untyped records (repo-frontend-p9-168, repo-frontend-p9-169). Plants' fit specs run against a 13-record stub book with no roles (repo-plantsfrontend-p6-064, repo-plantsfrontend-p6-083).

requirements.statement: Each party picker lists its addresses newest first, so an address just added through the address book appears at the top.
requirements.why: The prototype lists newly added addresses first, and the real picker already lists the book newest first.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p5-017 and trace-e2e-p9-030 show newest-first listing today.

requirements.statement: When a search matches no address, the picker shows 'No addresses match your search.' in place of the table, and still offers 'Save and continue'. The high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers show the same message.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 does not show an empty result; the real picker's message tells the trader why the list is empty, and nothing in the prototype contradicts it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-064 and trace-animals-fit-p15-015 show the message today.

requirements.statement: Every address-book read from the animals frontend is made on the server, for the signed-in session's organisation only, carrying that organisation in the Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header and the request tracing header; with no organisation in the session no read is made. The high-risk plants frontend's pickers likewise read only the signed-in organisation's book.
requirements.why: A real authorisation constraint: the address book trusts the organisation header, so the frontend's scoping is what keeps one organisation's addresses from another.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-155 to repo-frontend-p9-157 show this scoping today.

requirements.statement: A deleted address-book record is never offered on a picker; fetching one by id tells a deletion apart from a missing record, and any other failed address-book response is an error. The high-risk plants frontend's pickers behave the same: an outage is an error, never read as a deletion.
requirements.why: Deleted addresses must not be chosen again; the real service already relies on the address-book API for this.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-160 and repo-frontend-p9-163 show deleted records kept off the picker today.

requirements.statement: The animals frontend reads the address book and never writes to it; adding a record goes through the INS frontend, and the animals journey serves no create-address page of its own. The high-risk plants frontend's journey likewise only reads the book.
requirements.why: The INS frontend is the address book's only writer; how Design Release 2.1's in-journey add page is met belongs to the party-address-add-and-edit area.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-153 and repo-tests-p5-026 show the frontend reading only today.

requirements.statement: Every new or changed string on the roles and addresses page and the party pickers, and on the high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers, has a Welsh counterpart in the same change, still marked as a machine draft awaiting translator sign-off.
requirements.why: The real service is bilingual, and DR1 asked for each copy change in both languages; the prototype has no Welsh.
requirements.deltaNote: Today Welsh exists, as an unreviewed machine draft, only for the current strings (repo-frontend-p9-029, repo-frontend-p9-089). Plants' picker Welsh is likewise an unreviewed machine draft (repo-plantsfrontend-p6-047, repo-plantsfrontend-p6-059, repo-plantsfrontend-p6-049).

requirements.statement: The roles and addresses page, every animals party picker and the high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers have no serious or critical accessibility violations against WCAG 2.0, 2.1 A and AA and 2.2 AA, on first render and in their error states.
requirements.why: The real pages pass today and must keep passing as they change.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-176, repo-frontend-p9-188 and trace-animals-fit-p14-020 show clean axe scans today. repo-plantsfrontend-p6-078, repo-plantsfrontend-p6-078, repo-plantsfrontend-p6-087 and repo-plantsfrontend-p6-087 show plants' pickers clean today.

requirements.statement: The place of origin picker's search box shows the placeholder 'Search for a country'.

requirements.statement: On both animals sets, the place of origin picker's country search is the real frontend's accessible autocomplete over a native select of the countries MDM serves through reference-data, behaving as the real frontend configures it, with a button that submits the chosen country so the server narrows the rows to addresses in that country; submitting with no country shows every row. Without JavaScript the native select and the button do the same. Nothing beyond the component's own options is copied from the prototype's country widget.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 narrows the place of origin list by country. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm builds the no-JavaScript half now (inc-089) with the accessible autocomplete, whose entries come from MDM and whose mechanics follow the component, and keeps every search a form with a submit button, as DR1 also judged.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the place of origin picker has the same free-text server search as every other picker (repo-frontend-p9-055).

requirements.statement: The prototype's fixed demonstration addresses (nine places of origin, nine consignors, six consignees and importers, three places of destination) and its development socket polling are not built into the real service.
requirements.why: They are the prototype's seed data; the real pickers list the organisation's own address book.

requirements.statement: The prototype's page paths (/roles-and-addresses, /place-of-origin, /consignor-or-exporter, /consignee, /importer, /place-of-destination under /design-release-2.1) replace the real service's routes.
requirements.why: Out of scope: ruling sam-2026-10-09 says the prototype never decides URL paths and no increment changes an existing real path to match it; the real service keeps /addresses and its /select routes, in both the live-animals and the germinal-products sets.

requirements.statement: The roles and addresses page's Change links drop the visually hidden party name, as the prototype's do.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the prototype's identical 'Change' links are an accessibility gap a sighted user cannot see, not a design choice; the real links keep naming the party for screen-reader users.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: an add-address page served inside the live-animals journey at /<role path>/add-address that saves into the address book without the trader leaving the animals service.
requirements.why: Where the add page is served and which service writes the address book is cross-service behaviour the single-app prototype cannot express, so the INS frontend stays the address book's only writer, reached through the journey handshake; the animals frontend serves no /<role>/add-address page and its address-book service stays read-only (c-106).
requirements.deltaNote: Today 'Add a new address' links out to the INS frontend's /address-book/add (repo-frontend-p9-133, trace-e2e-p9-013), whose page sits in the INS layout (trace-e2e-p9-055-m1); the journey's own create page was retired and answers 404 (trace-e2e-p9-080).

requirements.statement: Every party picker (place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer and place of destination) and the consignment contact page has an 'Add a new address' link to the INS address book's /address-book/add, carrying journey-type 'gbn-ag', the notification reference, the role's fulfilment id (its obligation id) and a fresh handshake token, which the INS add page keeps as hidden fields and sends back unchanged; a role with no fulfilment mapping, or the frontend in stub mode, shows no add link.
requirements.why: The handshake is how the INS address book knows which notification and role to return the new address to; it stays because the INS frontend remains the address book's only writer (c-106). DR1 asked for a route to add an address from every address-selection page (inc-053), and it now exists.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today in ins-handshake.js (repo-frontend-p9-134, repo-frontend-p9-136): the pickers and the contact page link out with the four parameters (trace-e2e-p8-091, trace-e2e-p9-013), and the return is seen end to end (trace-e2e-p9-014, trace-e2e-p9-015, trace-e2e-p9-070-m1).

requirements.statement: The journey's address-return route accepts a return only when its fulfilment id names a role ('Unknown fulfilment' otherwise) and its handshake token matches the single-use token remembered in a cookie for that role ('Invalid handshake' otherwise, including a missing token), and looks the returned address id up in the signed-in organisation's own address book.
requirements.why: Stops a forged or replayed return from writing another organisation's address, or any address, into a notification.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today in address-return/controller.js (repo-frontend-p9-140, repo-frontend-p9-142, repo-frontend-p9-144).

requirements.statement: When a return cannot be completed, the trader goes back to the role's picker: an address that is not found or is deleted shows 'The address could not be found in your address book. Select another address or try adding it again.', and an address book that cannot be reached, or a save that fails, shows 'The address book could not be reached. Your answers on this page have been saved. Try again in a few minutes.'
requirements.why: A failed return must leave the trader somewhere they can carry on, with a reason they can act on.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today (repo-frontend-p9-145, repo-frontend-p9-146, repo-frontend-p9-150, repo-frontend-p9-151).

requirements.statement: A trader with no INS session who follows 'Add a new address' signs in through Defra ID first and then lands on the INS add page with the handshake intact.
requirements.why: The INS frontend owns its own session and stays the address book's only writer (c-106); crossing to it must not lose which notification and role the address is for.
requirements.deltaNote: Seen today end to end (trace-e2e-p9-052).

requirements.statement: Every add-address page that searches (the consignee, importer and place of destination pages reached from the journey, and the address book's 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' and 'Branch' add-details step) starts with a UK address search: a text field labelled 'Search for an address', placeholder 'Start typing...', browser autocomplete turned off, and a search icon button whose accessible name is 'Search', which submits the search to the server so it works without JavaScript.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 finds UK addresses by search rather than typing them in; every search is a form with a button that submits it, so the page works without JavaScript (ruling 2026-10-09 pm).
requirements.deltaNote: No address search exists today: the INS add page is typed in by hand (trace-e2e-p9-058).

requirements.statement: Submitting the address search lists matching UK addresses under 'Address search results', each a choice showing the organisation name and the full one-line address; Northern Ireland addresses are not offered.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's search results, in the version that works without JavaScript (ruling 2026-10-09 pm); results that appear as the trader types are a separate, design-blocked requirement.
requirements.blockedBy: The INS backend's address lookup becomes a real feature: today only the EUDPA-390 spike exists, gated to dev and local on a standalone page and not wired in. Once it lands the address search area is re-distilled (ruling 2026-10-09).

requirements.statement: The address search announces its result count to screen readers through a polite live region, such as '1 result available'.
requirements.why: Screen reader users must hear that results have appeared as they type; a custom announcement is JavaScript-only behaviour, so it waits on design as well as the lookup (ruling 2026-10-09 pm).

It is also blocked until the INS backend's address lookup becomes a real feature (today only the EUDPA-390 spike exists, gated to dev and local and not wired in), and the address search area is re-distilled once it lands.

requirements.statement: Picking a search result fills name, address line 1, address line 2, town or city and postcode with country United Kingdom, all still editable; email address and phone number stay empty for the trader to complete; any earlier error messages stay until the next submit.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's pick behaviour, in the version that works without JavaScript: the pick is submitted and the page comes back filled. Hiding the search box on a pick is part of the design-blocked search-only layout (req-653).

requirements.why: The prototype loses the locality because its form has no field for it; a saved address missing part of itself is a real data constraint the prototype cannot express.
requirements.blockedBy: The INS backend's address lookup becomes a real feature: today only the EUDPA-390 spike exists, gated to dev and local on a standalone page and not wired in. Once it lands the address search area is re-distilled (ruling 2026-10-09).

requirements.blockedBy: Design answers design question 10 (ruling 2026-10-09 pm): whether address search keeps a search-only layout that hides the address fields, or uses the GOV.UK address pattern with the fields always visible; this is one waiting-on-design increment. requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 reveals the form only once there is an address to complete; the search-only layout is design question 10's increment, because design is asked whether the GOV.UK address pattern with the fields always visible will do instead (ruling 2026-10-09 pm).
requirements.blockedBy: Design answers design question 10 (ruling 2026-10-09 pm): whether address search keeps a search-only layout that hides the address fields, or uses the GOV.UK address pattern with the fields always visible; this is one waiting-on-design increment. requirements.statement: Submitting a search page before picking or entering anything shows the six field errors in order ('Enter a name or organisation name', 'Enter address line 1', 'Enter a town or city', 'Enter a postcode or Zip code', 'Enter an email address', 'Enter a phone number'), with no country error and no error of the search's own, and reveals the fields so each error summary link reaches a visible field.

requirements.statement: The add-address page asks 'What else should this address be used for?' as a checkbox fieldset.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets one new address be saved for more roles than the one it was added from.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's INS add page has no such question (trace-e2e-p9-058 to trace-e2e-p9-067).

requirements.statement: The uses question's hint reads 'This address is being added as a <Role> address. Select any other roles or addresses this address should be used for.', naming the role's own label (Place of origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer or Place of destination) and using 'an' before Importer.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy; it tells the trader the role they came from is already implied.

requirements.statement: The uses checkboxes offer only the other roles on the same side, each labelled with the role name alone: place of origin offers 'Consignor'; consignor offers 'Place of origin'; consignee offers 'Importer' and 'Place of destination'; importer offers 'Consignee' and 'Place of destination'; place of destination offers 'Consignee' and 'Importer'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 never lets an origin-side address be marked for a destination-side role, or the other way round.

requirements.statement: No uses checkbox is preselected, ticking none raises no error, a value not offered for the role is discarded, and the ticked uses are kept when the page is shown again with errors.
requirements.why: The role the trader came from is implied; the extra uses are optional.

requirements.statement: An address added from the journey is saved in the address book carrying the role it was added for plus every use ticked, so the address book record holds its roles, in a field shape the address book service designs.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 saves the address with its types, and ruling 2026-10-09 keeps address uses and roles because a kept question must persist and DR1 asked for role-filtered pickers; today's record has no field to hold them, so the address book's persistence changes.
requirements.deltaNote: Today an address book record holds id, name, address fields, countryCode, phone, email, organisationId, deleted and timestamps, with no role or type (trace-e2e-p8-012).

requirements.statement: On the add-address page a blank name shows 'Enter a name or organisation name', linked to the name field.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's address book rules, which the journey copies, say 'Enter a name' (repo-frontend-p9-105, repo-frontend-p9-106); the INS add page's messages were never driven (trace-e2e-p9-069).

requirements.statement: On the add-address page a blank address line 1 shows 'Enter address line 1'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy, already used today.
requirements.deltaNote: The address book rules already say 'Enter address line 1' (repo-frontend-p9-108).

requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy, already used today.
requirements.deltaNote: The address book rules already say 'Enter a town or city' (repo-frontend-p9-111).

requirements.statement: On the add-address page a blank postcode shows 'Enter a postcode or Zip code'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's address book rules say 'Enter a postcode' (repo-frontend-p9-114).

requirements.statement: On the add-address page no country chosen shows 'Select a country'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's address book rules say 'Enter a country' (repo-frontend-p9-116).

requirements.statement: A failed submit of the add-address page shows an error summary titled 'There is a problem' listing every error in field order (seven on a blank manual page), each repeated inline with a visually hidden 'Error:' prefix and the field in its GOV.UK error style, and keeps everything the trader entered.
requirements.why: The GOV.UK error pattern, which Design Release 2.1 and today's address forms share.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's address forms already use this pattern (trace-e2e-p8-054, repo-tests-p5-067).

requirements.statement: The add-address page keeps the address book's length and format checks beyond the required-field checks: name and address lines 255 characters or fewer, town or city and county 100, postcode 12, phone 20, email 254 and in a valid format, each with today's message (such as 'Postcode must be 12 characters or fewer' and 'Enter an email address in the correct format').
requirements.why: The address book stores and validates these limits; a real validation constraint the prototype cannot express overrides its required-only checks.
requirements.deltaNote: The address book rules already carry these checks and messages (repo-frontend-p9-105, repo-frontend-p9-115, repo-frontend-p9-120; trace-e2e-p8-049, trace-e2e-p8-050).

requirements.statement: A refused add-address submit answers HTTP 400 and prefixes the browser title with 'Error: '.
requirements.why: The GOV.UK error pattern tells assistive technology the page holds errors; today's address forms already do it.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's address forms answer 400 with an 'Error: ' title (repo-frontend-p9-124, trace-e2e-p8-047-m1, trace-animals-fit-p15-062).

requirements.statement: The add-address page's fields carry browser autocomplete hints: organization for the name, address-line1, address-line2, address-level2 for town or city, postal-code, email and tel.
requirements.why: GOV.UK and WCAG 1.3.5 ask personal-data inputs to identify their purpose; the prototype leaves them out.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's INS add page sets autocomplete only on the email field (trace-e2e-p9-065); the journey's edit page already sets them all (repo-frontend-p9-103-m1).

requirements.statement: The add-address page's primary button reads 'Save and select'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the primary button reads 'Save and continue' (trace-e2e-p9-067).

requirements.statement: 'Save and select' saves the new address to the address book, puts a copy of it on the notification for the role it was added for, and returns the trader to the Consignment addresses page, where the role shows the address with a 'Change' link (after a consignee is saved this way, the unset importer and place of destination rows offer the 'Same as consignee' shortcut that page already carries, req-577 and req-578).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 finishes the role in one step.
requirements.deltaNote: Today saving returns the trader to the role's picker with the new address preselected ('Selected address: <name>'), and they press Save and continue to reach the hub (trace-e2e-p9-071, trace-e2e-p9-073, repo-tests-p5-029, repo-tests-p5-030).

requirements.statement: A secondary 'Save and return to address page' button saves the new address to the address book without selecting it, and returns the trader to the role's picker, where the new address is listed first.

requirements.deltaNote: Today the only secondary action is 'Cancel and return to address page' (trace-e2e-p9-067). The picker it lands on is the role-filtered, unpaginated picker the party picker area builds (ruling 2026-10-09 pm, inc-087).

requirements.statement: After either save, the page the trader lands on shows a GOV.UK notification banner titled 'Success' reading '<Name> address added to your address book', which stays on screen until the trader leaves or reloads the page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1, like DR1, confirms the address went into the address book; a message that leaves on a timer fails WCAG 2.2.1, so the banner stays and the INS frontend's script that hides it (address-book-success-banner.js) is removed (ruling 2026-10-09 pm).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the picker shows only the 'Selected address: <name>' inset, no banner (trace-e2e-p9-072).

requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy and destination.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a secondary 'Cancel and return to address page' button returns the trader to the role's picker, saving nothing (trace-e2e-p9-075, trace-e2e-p9-076, repo-tests-p5-031).

requirements.statement: An address added from the journey is saved into the signed-in organisation's address book with its email and phone, and is then listed in the address book and in every role picker.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree that a journey-added address joins the shared book.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the INS save creates the record in the organisation's book and the picker count rises (trace-e2e-p8-011, trace-e2e-p9-074).

requirements.statement: The add-address page is built from GOV.UK Frontend components (input, select, checkboxes, hint, error summary, notification banner, buttons, back link, width classes); the address search is the one component outside the toolbox, because GOV.UK Frontend has none.

requirements.deltaNote: Proven today (repo-tests-p5-037, repo-tests-p5-042, repo-tests-p5-044, trace-e2e-p8-001, trace-e2e-p8-006).

requirements.statement: On the review page each consignment party and the contact address read back as the name followed by the address lines and country (GB shown as 'United Kingdom'), each on its own line, without the telephone number or email address. In the same increment the plants frontend's check-answers place of destination, consignor and contact cards change the same way: they drop their 'Telephone number' and 'Email address' rows and read the address back one line per address line followed by the country, instead of joined by commas on one line.
requirements.why: The trader checks the copy the notification holds before submitting; plants has the same party cards, so it takes the same change at the same time (ruling 2026-10-09 pm), which withdraws plants' own d-013 addition of telephone and email to the contact card (c-293). The address-book record still carries both.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the review shows each copied address as a block, name in bold then each non-empty field on its own line, telephone and email included, under the 'Roles and addresses' and 'Contact address for this consignment' cards (trace-e2e-p8-004, trace-e2e-p8-018). Plants' party cards today carry Name, Address, Telephone number and Email address rows with the address joined by commas, and lose telephone and email and read line by line in the same increment (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-045); the plants repo claims that show today's cards sit in the party-cards area's working set, not this one.

requirements.statement: Each role and the consignment contact has its own page for editing the copy the notification holds: place-of-origin/edit, consignors/edit, consignees/edit, importers/edit, destinations/edit and consignment/contact/edit, reached from the hub's and review page's 'Edit details' links.
requirements.why: The address book accepts records that break the notification's address rules, so a notification needs a way to correct its own copy without touching the book: a real validation and cross-service constraint the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven today (repo-frontend-p9-091, repo-tests-p5-053, trace-e2e-p8-031). Design Release 2.1 shows no such page in this area; it is kept because rule-breaking copies need it (req-694).

requirements.why: Today's edit page copy.
