requirements.statement: The additional filters have a 'By arrival date' column of small GOV.UK radios 'Today', 'Tomorrow' and 'Next 7 days' (legend visually hidden, the same words shown as its heading); choosing one and searching lists only notifications arriving in that range, and the choice stays checked.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets a trader find what is arriving soon; the prototype's filter is inert, so the real service applies it.

requirements.statement: The additional filters have a 'By date range' column with the hint 'For example, 27/3/2026' and two MoJ date pickers, 'Start date' and 'End date' (a 'Choose date' calendar opening on the current month, weeks starting Monday, each a plain text field without JavaScript); the list shows only notifications arriving between the two dates, and the entered dates are kept.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's date range; it sits beside the arrival-date radios, so it filters the arrival date, as DR1's row also read it. The 9 October afternoon ruling accepts the MoJ date picker here, because the range is a search filter, not a date read from a document.

requirements.statement: When the start or end date cannot be read as a date, or the end date is before the start date, the list shows a GOV.UK error summary and an inline error on the date field ('Enter a real start date', 'Enter a real end date' or 'End date must be the same as or after the start date'), opens 'Additional filters', keeps the entered text in the 'Start date' and 'End date' pickers, and lists notifications without the date-range filter.
requirements.why: Validation is a real constraint the prototype cannot express, so a date the filter cannot use is answered with an error rather than silently ignored; the prototype still sets the labels and keeps the entered dates, and the GOV.UK date-input error pattern supplies the messages (c-166, which the 9 October afternoon ruling keeps).

requirements.statement: The additional filters have a 'Status' select offering exactly 'Select one', 'Action required', 'Submitted' and 'Completed'; choosing a status and searching lists only notifications in it, and the choice stays selected.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's status filter offers the statuses a trader acts on; drafts have their own tab, so Draft is not offered.

requirements.statement: The live animals list has three tabs, 'In progress', 'Draft' and 'Completed', built as MoJ sub navigation, each a link that loads the page with that tab chosen; 'In progress' is the list with no tab chosen, an unknown or missing tab shows 'In progress', and following a tab drops the search, sort and filters. The tab parameter's name and values are the animals frontend's.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 separates work in flight, unfinished drafts and finished notifications, and drafts keep a home on the list, which DR1 said must not be lost; the 9 October afternoon ruling builds the tabs as MoJ sub navigation on the animals frontend's own list, and the prototype never names query parameters (c-251).

requirements.statement: The 'In progress' tab lists submitted and action-required notifications, 'Draft' lists drafts and 'Completed' lists completed notifications.
requirements.why: Each tab holds the notifications at that stage, as Design Release 2.1 sets them out; a notification being amended goes in 'In progress' (c-165).

requirements.statement: A notification being amended is listed in the 'In progress' tab with today's yellow 'Amending' tag and its status-driven actions (Resume, Copy as new, Cancel amendment, Delete).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 has no amending state and its catch-all status mapping would file one as a draft only by fallback, while the backend persists an amendment as a submitted notification in AMEND that never returns to DRAFT and publishes it as an amendment of a submission: a persistence and cross-service constraint the prototype cannot express (c-165).
requirements.deltaNote: Today an amending notification is listed with every other notification, with a yellow 'Amending' tag; there are no tabs.

requirements.statement: Only the 'In progress' tab shows a count, in bold brackets, such as 'In progress (2)'; 'Draft' and 'Completed' show none, even when selected.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 counts only the notifications in flight; the count belongs to the tabs, which the 9 October afternoon ruling builds now, not to the blocked Summary cards.

requirements.statement: Under the tabs the cards sit under an h3 naming the tab: 'Notifications in progress', 'Draft notifications' or 'Completed notifications'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's subheading for each tab panel.

requirements.statement: The live animals list shows 8 notifications a page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's page size for every list; the 9 October afternoon ruling pages the reframed list 8 at a time.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page size comes from the listing: 25 from the animals backend (end-to-end) and 20 from the frontend stub (fit).

requirements.statement: A list of more than one page shows GOV.UK pagination with numbered page links, a 'Previous' link from page 2 and a 'Next' link before the last page; a list of one page, or no results, shows no pagination. This holds on the live animals list and on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 uses numbered pagination; today both lists have only Previous and Next. Plants takes the same paging in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today both lists use block-style pagination with only Previous and Next links and no page numbers.

requirements.statement: A page number below 1 or not a number shows page 1, and a page past the last shows the last page, on the live animals list as on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 clamps the page, so a stale or hand-typed page never shows an empty list; plants' list already does this.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the live animals list asked for a page past the last shows an empty page with 'Showing 0 of T Results' and only a Previous link; plants' list already clamps both ways (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-035).

requirements.statement: The live animals list's page links keep the tab (unless 'In progress'), the sort (unless the default), the search text and every additional filter.
requirements.why: Because the real search and filters apply, a page link that dropped them would show a different, unfiltered list on page 2 (c-163).
requirements.deltaNote: Today Previous and Next keep the sort (unless the default) and the reference search; there are no tabs or filters to keep.

requirements.statement: The list shows no results count: the 'Showing 1 Result', 'Showing S to E of T Results', 'Showing N of T Results' and 'No Results' line goes, from the live animals list and from plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's category list shows no results count; DR1 only deferred its rewrite of the count; plants takes the same frame.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a small bold line above both lists' cards reads 'No Results', 'Showing 1 Result', 'Showing N of T Results' or 'Showing S to E of T Results' (Welsh twins on plants).

requirements.statement: A search or filter that matches nothing shows an empty list with no message: the 'No notifications found' line goes, from the live animals list and from plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 has no empty-state message on any list; plants takes the same frame.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a search with no match on either list replaces the results line with 'No notifications found' and shows no cards.

requirements.statement: A tab or list with no notifications shows an empty list with no message: the sentence 'You have not started any notifications in this session.' goes, from the live animals list and from plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 has no empty-state message; today's sentence also wrongly says the animals list is session-scoped. Plants' own decision d-068 quoted the sentence, but the 9 October afternoon ruling gives plants the same frame (c-300).
requirements.deltaNote: Today a user with no notifications who is not searching sees 'You have not started any notifications in this session.' on both lists (Welsh 'Nid ydych wedi dechrau unrhyw hysbysiadau yn y sesiwn hon.' on plants).

requirements.statement: Each notification card on the live animals list and on plants' list is labelled for screen readers 'Notification <reference>' and has the reference as its h3.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's card names itself to assistive technology, and the 9 October afternoon ruling names the cards for screen readers in the reframed frame; the reference heading already exists on both lists.
requirements.deltaNote: Today each card on both lists is a GOV.UK summary card with the reference (or the journey id before one is issued) as its level-3 title, but no 'Notification <reference>' accessible name.

requirements.statement: A live animals card shows its facts in two rows: 'Commodity', 'Arrival date', 'Consignee' and 'Notification status', then the quantity, 'Origin', 'Consignor' and, when inspection is required, 'Inspection'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's card leads with what is coming, when, to whom and its status.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the card shows eight facts in three rows: Commodity, Origin, 'Arrival at destination'; Consignee, Consignor, Status; 'Date created', 'Date submitted'.

requirements.statement: The card labels the arrival date 'Arrival date', on the live animals list and on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label; DR1's own rename row was deferred, not judged; plants takes the same card layout.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the label is 'Arrival at destination' on the animals card and 'Arrival' on plants' card.

requirements.statement: The card labels the status 'Notification status', on the live animals list and on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label for the status fact; plants takes the same card layout.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the label is 'Status' on both cards.

requirements.statement: A live animals notification's card shows its quantity as 'Number of animals', from the notification's own count in the animals backend's record.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows how much is coming on every card; today no card shows a quantity, and the 9 October afternoon ruling takes the card's facts from the animals backend's record.

requirements.statement: The card shows no 'Date created' and no 'Date submitted', on the live animals list and on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's card has no dates other than arrival; today's 'Date submitted' is also blank on every card, submitted ones included, on both lists.
requirements.deltaNote: Today both cards show 'Date created' and 'Date submitted' (the latter blank in every end-to-end trace, and blank on plants' list in real mode because plants' list projection carries no submitted date; the animals list has the same hole).

requirements.statement: The card writes the arrival date as the day, the full month name and the year, such as '21 June 2026', on the live animals list and on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's card writes the arrival date with the full month name, in its code and its render alike, and nothing overrides the prototype here (c-164).
requirements.deltaNote: Today both cards write the arrival date as day, short month name and year, such as '7 Nov 2026'.

requirements.statement: A card whose notification has no commodity, no arrival date or no quantity yet shows 'Not applicable' for that fact instead of a blank value, on the live animals list and on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 never shows an empty fact; today a draft card is mostly empty labels.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a field with no answer yet is shown with an empty value and no placeholder on both lists.

requirements.statement: The live animals card's commodity is the notification's commodity name.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names the commodity as the trader chose it; germinal products need the product type as well as the species (req-1738).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the card shows the commodity's common name for its code (a commodity chosen as Bos taurus shows 'Cow').

requirements.statement: A draft's status is a 'Draft' tag and an action-required notification's an 'Action required' tag, while 'Submitted' is plain styled text, not a tag; plants' card follows the same styles for Draft and Submitted and keeps its 'Late' tag.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 uses a tag only for statuses that ask something of the trader; plants mirrors the components (c-301), and 'Action required' is animals only, because it rests on the ITAHC.
requirements.deltaNote: Today every status on both lists is a tag: Draft blue, Submitted green, Amending yellow (Deleted grey, never shown). The 'Completed' style is req-1739.

requirements.statement: A delayed notification shows a 'Delayed' tag on an error card with the reason for the delay; the prototype's placeholder text 'Error message' is not copied.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows delays on the list; its message is placeholder copy.
requirements.blockedBy: The authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) sends post-submission outcomes (action required with its reason, inspection required, delayed, completed) back to the notification record; no delay status or reason reaches the service today.

requirements.statement: A notification the authorities have finished with shows the status 'Completed' and is listed in the 'Completed' tab.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 moves finished notifications out of the in-progress list; the completed status waits for a real source of completion.
requirements.blockedBy: The authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) sends post-submission outcomes (action required with its reason, inspection required, delayed, completed) back to the notification record; no completed status reaches the service today.

requirements.statement: A notification chosen for inspection shows an extra 'Inspection' fact with a 'Required' tag at the end of the card's second row.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 warns the trader on the list that the consignment will be inspected.
requirements.blockedBy: The authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) sends post-submission outcomes (action required with its reason, inspection required, delayed, completed) back to the notification record; no inspection decision reaches the service today.

requirements.statement: A live animals card keeps its status-driven actions, each named for screen readers with ' notification <reference>': a draft offers Resume, 'Copy as new' and Delete; a submitted notification offers View, Amend, 'Copy as new' and Delete; a notification being amended offers Resume, 'Copy as new', 'Cancel amendment' and Delete. Amend and 'Copy as new' stay link-styled buttons that post, in the same typeface as the links.
requirements.why: DR1 judged that the card keeps its status-driven links rather than DR1's flat 'Copy as new' and 'View', and that judgement wins over Design Release 2.1's same flat pair. Without it a trader could not resume a draft from the list.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-047, p3-050 and p3-052 (proven by trace-animals-fit-p2-037, p2-042 and p2-044): the card already offers these sets in this order, with visually hidden ' notification <reference>' text.

requirements.statement: A card in a status the real service does not have today (delayed or completed, and action required where it has no status-driven set of its own) offers 'Copy as new' then 'View', View opening the notification's review page.
requirements.why: DR1's judgement covers only the card links built today; for the new statuses nothing overrides Design Release 2.1, whose card offers 'Copy as new' and 'View'.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a notification in any status other than Draft, Submitted or Amending has no actions on its card.
requirements.blockedBy: The authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) sends post-submission outcomes (action required with its reason, inspection required, delayed, completed) back to the notification record; until it does, no card is in these statuses.

requirements.statement: After an action that sends the trader back to the list with that action's flag on the redirect (such as a delete), the list shows a GOV.UK success notification banner with role alert, titled 'Success', carrying that action's message; plants' deletion banner takes the same 'Success' title. The new wording is added in each list feature's own copy: the shared notificationActions wording, which other pages also use, is not reworded in place.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 uses one success banner titled 'Success'; the message itself is set by the action. The 9 October ruling keeps the flag on the redirect (such as ?deleted=1) rather than a message held for the trader (c-252), and the afternoon ruling gives plants' banner the same title in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the banners are titled for the action: 'Notification deleted' with 'The notification has been deleted.' on both lists, and 'Notification copied' with 'A new draft notification has been created.' on the animals list (never reached).

requirements.statement: The success message is held for the trader and shown once, then cleared, rather than shown whenever the list's address carries a flag such as ?deleted=1.
requirements.why: The 2026-10-09 ruling drops moving the success banner to a message held for the trader and shown once (req-1087, inc-140 criteria 2 and 3): the flag on the redirect, such as ?deleted=1, stays, so the banner shows whenever the list is opened with it (c-252).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the banners show whenever the dashboard is opened with ?deleted=1 or ?copied=1, and that stays.

requirements.statement: The notification list's success banner, the deletion message included, does not dismiss itself on the live animals list or on plants' list: it stays until the trader leaves or reloads the page.
requirements.why: A message that disappears on a timer can vanish before a screen reader or a slow reader reaches it (WCAG 2.2.1); this accessibility duty overrides Design Release 2.1's 5-second auto-dismiss, and the 9 October afternoon ruling confirms it (c-006).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-062, repo-frontend-p3-065 and repo-plantsfrontend-p3-066: today's deletion banners are GOV.UK success banners announced as alerts, with no timer that dismisses them.

requirements.statement: The live animals list keeps its stale-action banner ('The notification has been updated' / 'This notification was updated since you opened it. Review the details and try again.') and its 'There is a problem' banner when a copy from the list fails.
requirements.why: Concurrency and failure handling are real constraints the prototype cannot express, so they stay although Design Release 2.1 shows neither.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-067 and repo-frontend-p3-066: the dashboard shows the stale-action banner with ?staleAction=1 and the 'There is a problem' banner with HTTP 500 after a failed copy.

requirements.statement: Every list string has a Welsh version, on the animals lists and on plants' list, marked as a machine draft that ships only after a translator signs it off under the Welsh Language Standards.
requirements.why: Both real services are bilingual and their dashboard Welsh is an unreviewed machine draft; Design Release 2.1's new strings need Welsh twins too.
requirements.deltaNote: Today every English dashboard key on both lists has a machine-drafted Welsh twin, not yet reviewed by a translator; plants' English dashboard copy is also marked provisional.

requirements.statement: The live animals list has no serious or critical WCAG 2 A or AA axe violations, empty or with cards, and does not scroll sideways at 1280px or at 769px wide; plants' list has no serious or critical WCAG 2 A or AA axe violations.
requirements.why: Both real lists meet this today and the reframed lists must keep meeting it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-118, p3-119, p3-108 and repo-plantsfrontend-p3-081: fit tests prove no serious or critical axe violations, and no sideways scroll on the animals list.

requirements.statement: The germinal products set's root in the animals frontend renders its own copy of the reframed list: the caption 'Dashboard', the h1 'Germinal products', the same search, sort, additional filters and tabs pointed at its own address, and a 'Create new' button that starts a germinal products notification in the germinal products set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives each category of animal notification its own list; the 9 October afternoon ruling builds the germinal list as the germinal set's own copy of the reframed live animals list (inc-141), instead of an INS germinal list.

requirements.statement: The live animals list shows only live animals notifications: a germinal products notification never appears on it, and a notification whose record holds no category counts as live animals.
requirements.why: A trader looking at one category must not see another's notifications; the animals backend stores each notification's category on its record, an absent category meaning live animals, and the reframed list reads that record.

requirements.statement: Deleted notifications never appear on any list or in a search.
requirements.why: A deleted notification is gone for the trader; both Design Release 2.1 and the real services leave it out.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p3-002, repo-frontend-p3-025 and repo-plantsfrontend-p3-044: the animals backend's list leaves out DELETED notifications, and both frontends filter them out.

requirements.statement: A newly started notification appears on the list straight away.
requirements.why: A trader must find their new draft on the list as soon as they have started it; the list reads the animals backend's own record, not an event-populated read model that lags writes.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p4-002 and trace-e2e-p3-049: a newly started notification is found on the dashboard by its reference.

requirements.statement: A list shows only the notifications of the signed-in trader's organisation, and the animals backend's list API refuses a caller that does not say which organisation it acts for.
requirements.why: Authentication and data separation are real constraints the prototype cannot express; today the animals backend's list serves every trader's notifications to every caller, while plants' list is already limited to the session organisation's known notifications.

requirements.statement: The INS backend's notification read model and its GET /notifications list API (its record fields, event handling, paging, sorts, reference search and scoping) are not changed for the notification lists: the lists no longer read them in this programme.
requirements.why: The 9 October afternoon ruling builds the reframed lists on the animals frontend and animals backend and drops the INS read model's part of the list rows; the INS dashboard that does read it is blocked until its requirements firm up, and its category gap (germinal notifications listed without their category) is a known gap until then.
requirements.deltaNote: Recorded from the INS backend as it is today.

requirements.statement: The animals backend's list returns, for each notification, what the card shows: its category and its number of animals, or for germinal products its number of packages and each line's species and product type, beside the reference number, status, commodity name, arrival date, origin, consignee name and consignor name it returns today, with a missing fact returned as empty.
requirements.why: The card cannot show facts its list API does not return; the 9 October afternoon ruling takes the card facts from the animals backend's record, and that list item carries no category or quantity today.
requirements.deltaNote: Today each animals backend list item carries the reference number, concurrency token, status, created timestamp, origin, commodity, consignor, consignee and transport, but no category or quantity of its own.

requirements.statement: The animals backend's list API filters by category (live animals or germinal products, absent meaning live animals) and by tab (the in-progress statuses, drafts, or completed), and reports how many notifications the 'In progress' tab holds.
requirements.why: Each set's list and each tab shows only its own notifications, and the 'In progress' tab shows its count; with both lists built on the animals backend, the category filter belongs to its list (c-159).

requirements.statement: The animals backend's list API takes a search text and returns every notification whose reference number, commodity, consignee or consignor contains it, ignoring case and surrounding spaces, paged like any other list.
requirements.why: The list's search matches a keyword across those facts; today the list API matches only one exact, case-sensitive, whole reference and returns at most one notification.
requirements.deltaNote: Today referenceNumber is trimmed and matched exactly against a whole reference; a match holds exactly one notification, and a miss answers 200 with an empty page.

requirements.statement: The animals backend's list API filters by status and by an arrival-date range (from and to dates, either optional).
requirements.why: The status select and both arrival-date filters need the API to narrow the list; today the list API has no filter beyond an exact reference.

requirements.statement: The animals backend's list API sorts by creation date (newest or oldest first) and by arrival date, defaults to arrival date newest first, and breaks ties on a second key so no notification repeats or goes missing between pages.
requirements.why: 'Newest first' and 'Oldest first' order by creation date and 'Arrival date' by arrival; a single-key sort with ties (such as drafts with no arrival date) is unstable across pages.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the animals backend already sorts on arrivalDate or createdAt, defaulting to arrival date newest first, but on one field only, with no tie-breaker.

requirements.statement: The animals backend's list API serves 8 notifications a page, numbered from 1, and reports the page, size, number of elements, total elements and total pages.
requirements.why: The list shows 8 a page and builds numbered pagination from the totals.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the animals backend serves 25 a page, set by configuration; the response shape and the 1-based page already exist.

requirements.statement: The INS backend's list API answers a bad request, such as a page below 1, with a 400 validation problem response naming the field, and an unexpected failure with a 500 problem response that hides the underlying error.
requirements.why: This is the INS list API's behaviour today; the notification lists no longer call that API in this programme (req-1097), so nothing here is built or changed.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insbackend-p1-029 and p1-104: a page below 1 answers 400 'Validation Error' with an errors map keyed 'page', proven by repo-insbackend-p1-118.

requirements.statement: Read-model defects and operational details the design release does not touch stay as they are and go to the report: a non-numeric page likely answering 500, a shared reference likely answering 500, failed events never retried and so lost, no dead-letter queue shown, untested lastUpdated sorts and deletion end to end, the metrics, logging, port, switched-off OpenAPI, template README, empty seed, missing rulings ledger and the absence of a get-one endpoint.
requirements.why: None of these is a difference from Design Release 2.1; the programme does not fix them, so they are reported rather than built.
requirements.deltaNote: Recorded from the INS backend as it is today.

requirements.statement: The prototype's demo data is not built: its seeded notifications and their fixed references, the states it fakes by a notification's position (action required, status changes, delays, inspection, Plants), its placeholder number of animals, its demo consignee and consignor names, its fixed commodity-code look-up, its category guess for unlabelled notifications and its session ordering of drafts, submissions and seeds.
requirements.why: These are demonstration mechanics of the prototype, not rules for the real service, which holds real notifications with their own facts and statuses.

requirements.statement: The prototype's list with no category is not built: its fallback heading 'Live animals and germinal products', its 'By type' select (shown only without a category, hiding Plants) and its uncategorised 'View tasks' and 'View updates' links; no list combines categories, and plants' list stays plants only.
requirements.why: The rulings keep each notification list in its own frontend for its own set, and the afternoon ruling says this programme no longer builds the INS notification lists the overall home linked to, so a list combining categories has no place; plants' own decisions keep its list plants only and treat the Design Release 2 cross-journey dashboard as evidence for a later INS front door.

requirements.statement: The address book lives in the INS frontend at /address-book, reached from an 'Address book' item in the service navigation, and that item is marked active (aria-current) on the list, view and delete pages. 'Log out' stays in the navigation.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 puts the address book behind the service navigation; DR1's inc-062 ruling already placed the real book in the INS front door rather than the animals frontend.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS frontend serves the list at /address-book (repo-insfrontend-p2-001), its navigation links to it and marks it active on the list, view and delete pages (trace-ins-fit-p2-004, trace-ins-fit-p2-007, trace-ins-fit-p3-069), and the animals dashboard links across to it (repo-tests-p5-001). The navigation's Templates item belongs to the shared layout area.

requirements.statement: A signed-out user opening any address book page is sent to sign in and returned to the page they asked for; a signed-in session with no organisation is refused.
requirements.why: The real address book holds an organisation's records, so it needs an authenticated organisation; the prototype cannot express sign-in.
requirements.deltaNote: Signed-out requests to /address-book and /address-book/add redirect to /auth/sign-in with the path as redirect (trace-e2e-p15-010, trace-e2e-p15-011); a session without an organisation gets 403 (repo-insfrontend-p2-002).

requirements.statement: Address book page titles read '<page heading> - Import notification service - GOV.UK': 'Address book - Import notification service - GOV.UK' on the list, '<address name> - Import notification service - GOV.UK' on the view page and 'Delete this address? - Import notification service - GOV.UK' on the delete page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 titles every page with the GOV.UK suffix and a hyphen separator.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the titles are 'Address book | Import notification service', '<name> | Import notification service' and 'Delete address | Import notification service' (trace-ins-fit-p2-008, trace-ins-fit-p2-037, trace-ins-fit-p3-047): a pipe separator and no GOV.UK suffix.

requirements.statement: The list page's heading is 'Address book'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS list's h1 is 'Address book' (repo-insfrontend-p2-003, trace-ins-fit-p2-009).

requirements.statement: Under the heading the list page shows, in large body text, 'Manage your addresses for use across all your import notifications'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's intro wording.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the intro reads 'Manage addresses used across import and export services.' in normal body text (repo-insfrontend-p2-004, trace-ins-fit-p2-010).

requirements.statement: The list page has an 'Add a new address' button (a link styled as a button) to /address-book/add, shown whatever the list holds.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS list always shows 'Add a new address' to /address-book/add (repo-insfrontend-p2-010, trace-ins-fit-p2-013).

requirements.statement: On the list page the 'Add a new address' button comes directly under the intro, above the 'Filter addresses' panel and the category tabs.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's order puts adding first and filtering below it.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the search form sits between the intro and the 'Add a new address' button (repo-insfrontend-p2-005, repo-insfrontend-p2-010).

requirements.statement: Search and the Type filter sit inside a collapsible 'Filter addresses' disclosure with a chevron, collapsed when the list loads, so the search field is hidden until the user opens it. It is the GOV.UK details component, styled to match the design, so it opens and closes without JavaScript.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 tucks filtering away behind one disclosure.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the search form is always visible with no disclosure (repo-insfrontend-p2-005), and the pages use govuk-frontend components only (trace-e2e-p15-037).

requirements.statement: The search field is labelled 'Search'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the field is labelled 'Search addresses' (repo-insfrontend-p2-005, trace-e2e-p15-023).

requirements.statement: The search field's placeholder is 'Search by name, address or country', and it has no hint.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 guides the search with a placeholder, not a hint.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the code carries a hint 'Search by name, town or city, postcode or country', passed where the input macro most likely does not render it, and no placeholder (repo-insfrontend-p2-006).

requirements.statement: The search field has an icon-only search button whose accessible name is 'Search', in place of a visible 'Search' text button. It is a real submit button of the filter form, so pressing it, or pressing Enter in the search field, submits the form with or without JavaScript.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's search control.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a primary text button 'Search' submits the form (repo-insfrontend-p2-007, trace-e2e-p9-089). The prototype's icon button is type=button and submits nothing (c-169); the real one submits.

requirements.statement: Search matches the trimmed text, case-insensitively and anywhere inside a word, against an address's name, type labels, every address line (line 1, line 2, town or city, county, postcode), its transporter approval number and its country name; a blank search is no search.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 searches the whole visible row, so 'Ballymore' or a country finds the entry; today only name, town and postcode match.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the address book API's q matches only name, town or city and postcode (repo-addressbook-p3-032, repo-addressbook-p3-033, and the k6 suite's worst-case search is built on that, repo-perftests-p2-023), and a country is found only when the whole term resolves to a country name, which the INS frontend turns into an OR countryCode filter (repo-insfrontend-p2-009). Case-insensitive, partial, literal, trimmed matching that leaves out deleted and other organisations' addresses already holds (repo-addressbook-p3-034 to p3-039, repo-addressbook-p3-067).

requirements.statement: The address book API keeps its countryCode filter as it is: an exact, trimmed ISO alpha-2 code, ignored when blank, organisation-scoped, leaving out deleted addresses, and combined with q by OR.
requirements.why: The locked contract and ruling cv-048 fix these semantics; nothing in Design Release 2.1 asks to change them.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven by the address book's AddressSearchIT and OperatorServiceTest (repo-addressbook-p3-064 to p3-066, repo-addressbook-p3-074, repo-addressbook-p3-075).

requirements.statement: The address book filter stays a GET form to the address book list carrying the selected tab, the search and the Type filter, and the address book API filters the whole category by the search and type and returns 8 a page. The search parameter keeps today's name, q; the parameter that carries the tab and the values it takes, and the type parameter, are the INS service's to name, not the prototype's. Pressing the search button, or pressing Enter in the search field or on the Type select, submits the form; changing the Type select submits nothing by itself. The page works fully without JavaScript, and no script re-requests the list as the user types (that waits on design, req-2039). The same holds locally, in the stub, on the compose stack and in CDP.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 filters live across the whole category with no apply button, and the prototype wins on that look and feel; the real address book is paged on the server and cannot be asked for a whole category, a constraint that overrides only the prototype's way of holding every row in the page (c-169). Sam's 9 October ruling keeps these server-side filters and leaves parameter names to the INS service.
requirements.deltaNote: Today search is a server-side GET form submitted by a Search button, carrying only q, and the API answers one server-sized page at a time (repo-insfrontend-p2-005, repo-insfrontend-p2-068, repo-addressbook-p3-010): there is no tab or type to carry or filter by.

requirements.statement: While a search or Type filter is active, the submitted list's results line counts the matches (for example 'Showing 1-2 of 2'), and pagination shows only when the matches run past one page of 8.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps the count true to what is shown while filtering and hides pagination unless the matches need it; nothing the server-paged constraint forces changes that (c-169).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the results line already counts only matches after a submitted search (repo-addressbook-p3-047, repo-insfrontend-p2-014), but there is no Type filter to count, and pagination starts past 25 rather than 8 (req-1141).

requirements.statement: The list is split into category tabs, in this order: 'Origin and Consignor', 'Destination, Consignee and Importer' and 'Branch' (the 'Transporter' tab, between the second and Branch, waits with transporter management: req-2040). The tabs are the Ministry of Justice sub navigation component, each a link that loads the address book list on that tab, with the selected one marked; the INS frontend adds the @ministryofjustice/frontend package at the same major version as the animals frontend. The query parameter that carries the tab, and its values, are the INS service's to name.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 groups addresses by what they are used for.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the list is one table with no tabs (trace-e2e-p15-026), the API has no type or usage filter to split by (repo-addressbook-p3-046), and the INS frontend has no MoJ frontend package. The address type each record carries comes from the add-and-edit area's typed record.

requirements.statement: Each tab panel has its own heading: 'Origin and Consignor addresses', 'Destination, Consignee and Importer addresses' or 'Branch addresses' ('Transporter addresses' waits with the Transporter tab, req-2040).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 heads each category's table.

requirements.statement: An address appears on every tab whose category holds any of its types: Origin and Consignor holds place of origin, consignor, consignor or exporter and exporter; Destination, Consignee and Importer holds consignee, importer, place of destination, contact and packer; Branch holds branch addresses. So an address with several types can appear on more than one tab, and the list API can return one category's addresses. The Transporter category waits with the Transporter tab (req-2040). How the address record holds its types is the address book service's design.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lists an organisation under each use it is held for.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's record carries no type (repo-tests-p5-095, trace-e2e-p15-082, repo-insfrontend-p2-070) and the list has no type or category filter (repo-addressbook-p3-046).

requirements.statement: With no tab chosen in the request, or an unknown one, the list opens on the Origin and Consignor tab.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's default tab.

requirements.statement: Each tab link goes to page 1 of that category, keeps the current search and drops the Type filter; the filter form carries the selected tab as a hidden field so filtering stays on the current tab.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps a search across tabs but not a type, which is per category.

requirements.statement: The legacy category values origin-and-sender and destination-and-receiver are not accepted as aliases.
requirements.why: They exist only so the prototype's older design releases keep working; the real service never used those values, so there are no links to keep alive.

requirements.statement: The filter has a select labelled 'Type' whose first option is 'Select one' (empty value), then options for the current tab only: 'Place of Origin' and 'Consignor' on Origin and Consignor; 'Consignee', 'Importer' and 'Place of Destination' on Destination, Consignee and Importer; 'Branch Address' on Branch. The Transporter tab's 'Commercial' and 'Private' wait with that tab (req-2041).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 narrows a tab by type.
requirements.deltaNote: Today there is no type filter in the page or the API (repo-addressbook-p3-046).

requirements.statement: The Type filter keeps an address when one of its types equals the choice; the list API takes the type and category so the filter runs over the whole category on the server, still organisation-scoped and without deleted addresses. How the record and the API carry type and category is the address book service's design. Filtering transporters by transporter type waits with the Transporter tab (req-2041).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's type matching, delivered over the real, paged book.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the list API's only filters are q and countryCode, every path pinned to ACTIVE and the caller's organisation (repo-addressbook-p3-046, repo-addressbook-p3-027).

requirements.statement: Above the table a results line reads 'Showing <start>-<end> of <total>'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS list shows 'Showing <from>-<to> of <total>' (repo-insfrontend-p2-014, trace-ins-fit-p2-015).

requirements.statement: When nothing matches, or the book or tab is empty, the list shows 'Showing 0 of 0' and an empty table, with no empty-state or no-match message.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows the same table whatever it holds.
requirements.deltaNote: Today an empty book shows 'You have no addresses yet.' and a search with no match shows 'No addresses match "<term>".', each in place of the table and with no results line (repo-insfrontend-p2-012, repo-insfrontend-p2-013, trace-ins-fit-p2-034).

requirements.statement: The list has no 'Clear search' link; the user clears the search field instead.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's filter has no clear control.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a 'Clear search' link to /address-book shows above the results of a search and under a no-match message (repo-insfrontend-p2-013, repo-insfrontend-p2-015).

requirements.statement: On every tab except Transporter the table's columns are Name, Type, Address and Country, then an action column whose header 'Action' is visually hidden.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows what each address is used for.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the columns are Name, Address, Country and the hidden Action, with no Type column (repo-insfrontend-p2-016, trace-e2e-p15-026).

requirements.statement: On the Transporter tab the table's columns are Name, Address, Approval number and Type, then the hidden Action column, with no Country column: the country is the address's last line, the approval number reads like 'RO/BUCHAREST/T1/00092010', and Type is 'Commercial' or 'Private'. Built with the Transporter tab once transporter management is decided.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows transporters by approval and type.
requirements.blockedBy: The product owner decides whether the service manages transporters and, if so, whether in the address book (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm, transporter management); the transporter area is then re-distilled.

requirements.statement: In the Name column a name of more than one word is shown on two lines: the first word, then the rest.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's Name cell.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the Name cell shows the name on one line (repo-insfrontend-p2-017).

requirements.statement: In the Address column every stored address line (line 1, line 2, town or city, county, postcode) is shown on its own line, each but the last ending in a comma; blank lines are left out.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows the whole address, line by line.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the cell joins only address line 1, town or city and postcode into one comma-separated line, leaving out line 2 and county (repo-insfrontend-p2-018, trace-e2e-p15-027).

requirements.statement: The Country column shows the country's name, not its code.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS list looks up the country name, falling back to the code (repo-insfrontend-p2-019, trace-e2e-p15-028).

requirements.statement: The Type column shows the address's type labels joined by ', ', using the list's labels: 'Place of origin', 'Consignor' (for consignor, consignor or exporter and exporter), 'Consignee', 'Importer', 'Place of destination', 'Branch', 'Contact address' and 'Packer'. These differ in case and wording from the Type filter's options. The 'Transporter' label waits with the Transporter tab (req-2040).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 labels uses in sentence case in the table.

requirements.statement: Each row ends with a 'View' link to /address-book/{id}; its accessible name adds the address's name in visually hidden text ('View <name>').
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's row action; the hidden name keeps each link distinct for screen reader users.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS list already ends each row with 'View' plus the hidden name (repo-insfrontend-p2-020, trace-ins-fit-p2-021).

requirements.statement: The list shows 8 addresses a page, set through the address book service's server-side page size setting.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 pages at 8; ruling cv-025 keeps page size a server setting, so the setting changes rather than the contract.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the address book pages at 25 because address-book.list.page-size is unset (repo-addressbook-p3-011), and the INS list shows 25 a page (trace-ins-fit-p2-023, trace-e2e-p15-030).

requirements.statement: When there is more than one page, GOV.UK pagination shows a numbered link to every page with the current one marked, 'Previous' except on the first page and 'Next' except on the last; with one page there is no pagination.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS list already renders GOV.UK pagination this way (repo-insfrontend-p2-021, trace-ins-fit-p2-024 to p2-029).

requirements.statement: Pagination links keep the category, search and Type filter, and add page only for pages after the first.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps the user's tab and filters as they page.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the links keep q and countryCode and add page only after the first (repo-insfrontend-p2-022); there is no category or type to keep.

requirements.statement: A page number below 1 or not a number shows page 1, and one beyond the last page shows the last page's addresses.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 never shows an empty page for a stale page link.
requirements.deltaNote: A missing, non-numeric or sub-1 page already means page 1 (repo-insfrontend-p2-011), but a page beyond the last gets an empty items list from the API (repo-addressbook-p3-017) while only the label and pagination are clamped (repo-insfrontend-p2-023).

requirements.statement: The list shows the newest address first, with a stable order from page to page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lists the user's latest additions first; the real API already sorts newest first.
requirements.deltaNote: The API sorts by creation time, newest first, ties by id (repo-addressbook-p3-028, repo-addressbook-p3-029); a newly saved address lands in the first row (trace-e2e-p15-031).

requirements.statement: After an add, edit or delete the list shows a GOV.UK success notification banner titled 'Success' above the heading, once: it is cleared when read.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS list shows the session's success message once in a 'Success' banner (repo-insfrontend-p2-028, repo-insfrontend-p2-029), after a delete and after an add or edit (trace-e2e-p15-033, trace-e2e-p15-034). The add and edit banner wording belongs to the add-and-edit area (req-1260, req-1277).

requirements.statement: The success banner stays on the page until the user leaves or reloads it; it does not hide itself after a few seconds, and the INS frontend's address-book-success-banner.js, which hides it, is removed.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's banner stays until the user moves on, so slower readers do not miss it.
requirements.deltaNote: Today client JavaScript (address-book-success-banner.js) hides the banner 3 seconds after load (repo-insfrontend-p2-030); WCAG 2.2.1 rules out a message that leaves on a timer.

requirements.statement: After a delete the banner reads '<Name> address deleted', with the name's first letter capitalised and the rest lower-cased (for example 'Green valley farm address deleted'), or 'Address deleted' when the name is blank.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's delete confirmation wording.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the banner reads '<name> deleted from your address book', name as typed (repo-insfrontend-p2-031, trace-e2e-p15-035).

requirements.statement: The address book is stored by the address book service and belongs to the organisation: every user signed in to the same organisation sees the same addresses, and one user's additions and deletions show for the others.
requirements.why: Persistence and organisation scoping are real constraints the prototype, which holds the book in one user's session, cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: The service scopes by organisation only, with no user identity (repo-addressbook-p4-003); E2E proves another user in the organisation sees adds and deletes (trace-e2e-p15-077, trace-e2e-p15-078).

requirements.statement: Address book additions, edits and deletions held only in the user's session, with no address book API behind them.
requirements.why: Set aside by c-172: the real book is persisted and organisation-wide.

requirements.statement: No caller can list, read or delete another organisation's addresses: the path organisation must match the caller's organisation header exactly, and any miss, whether unknown or another organisation's, is the same 404, never 403.
requirements.why: Organisation isolation and non-disclosure are real authorisation constraints (rulings cv-010 and cv-040).
requirements.deltaNote: Proven in the address book's AddressScopingIT and IdentityHeaderFilterTest (repo-addressbook-p4-053, repo-addressbook-p4-054, repo-addressbook-p4-059); no E2E spec signs in as a second organisation (repo-tests-p5-097).

requirements.statement: Every address book API call must carry a well-formed Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header (1 to 64 letters, digits, underscores or hyphens); a missing, blank or malformed one is refused with a 400 problem response with no errors map, before any handler runs, and a new address is stamped with that organisation.
requirements.why: The header is the address book's only tenant key.
requirements.deltaNote: IdentityHeaderFilter enforces it on every /organisation/ path (repo-addressbook-p4-006, repo-addressbook-p4-010, repo-addressbook-p4-044).

requirements.statement: The INS frontend calls the address book server-side under /organisation/{orgId}/addresses with the signed-in session's organisation in the Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header and the trace id, and refuses to call it without an organisation.
requirements.why: The address book trusts the header alone, so it must come only from the authenticated session (ruling cv-010).
requirements.deltaNote: The INS client sets the header from the session and fails before sending without one (repo-insfrontend-p2-065, repo-insfrontend-p2-067).

requirements.statement: The address book's trust boundary outside the service: stripping a client-sent organisation header, setting it from the verified session, CDP network policy, and the service's own resource-server authentication.
requirements.why: Platform and deployment controls the Design Release 2.1 programme does not change; it goes to the report as a standing risk nothing in the repo proves.

requirements.statement: The address book service logs each request with the caller's organisation id and no address personal data, logs list requests without the search term, and times the list endpoint and its query as metrics.
requirements.why: Operability without leaking personal data.
requirements.deltaNote: IdentityHeaderFilter and OperatorController already do this (repo-addressbook-p4-036, repo-addressbook-p3-048, repo-addressbook-p3-049).

requirements.statement: The list API (GET /organisation/{orgId}/addresses) returns a camelCase page object with items, page, pageSize, totalItems and totalPages, holds only live addresses, and answers errors as application/problem+json.
requirements.why: The real list contract the INS frontend reads.
requirements.deltaNote: OperatorPageResponse and OperatorListIT (repo-addressbook-p3-018, repo-addressbook-p3-053).

requirements.statement: Reading one address by id returns it with every stored field, including a deleted one with deleted true; only that tells a caller the address was deleted, and a 404 means unknown or not this organisation's.
requirements.why: Notifications keep referring to addresses after they are deleted, so deletion must stay detectable.
requirements.deltaNote: AddressGetIT proves 200 with deleted true for a tombstone and 404 for an unknown id (repo-addressbook-p2-033, repo-addressbook-p2-034).

requirements.statement: Deleting an address removes it from the list and search for everyone in the organisation but keeps it as a tombstone (deleted, name intact, readable by id); delete answers 204, is idempotent, cannot be undone, and is reached in the interface only through the delete confirmation page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 removes the address from the book; the tombstone is the real persistence constraint that stops notifications referencing it from dangling.
requirements.deltaNote: The service soft-deletes and answers 204 idempotently (repo-addressbook-p2-053, repo-addressbook-p2-058); E2E proves the tombstone (trace-e2e-p15-075).

requirements.statement: The address view page is at /address-book/{id}, headed with the address's name, and can be opened directly by its URL.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS view page is served at /address-book/{id} with the name as h1 (repo-insfrontend-p2-032, repo-insfrontend-p2-038).

requirements.statement: The view page's summary list always shows, in this order, 'Name or organisation name', 'Address line 1', 'Town or city', 'Postcode or Zip code', 'Country' (as a name), 'Email address' and 'Phone number'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree on these rows.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS view page shows these rows in this order (repo-insfrontend-p2-040, trace-ins-fit-p2-039).

requirements.statement: The view page shows 'Address line 2 (optional)' after Address line 1, and the county row after Town or city, only when they have a value.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 leaves empty optional rows out.
requirements.deltaNote: Today both rows always show, blank when empty (repo-insfrontend-p2-049, trace-ins-fit-p2-041).

requirements.statement: The view page's county row is labelled 'County (optional)'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the row is labelled 'County' (repo-insfrontend-p2-045, trace-ins-fit-p2-042).

requirements.statement: The view page does not show the address's types or uses, and its summary rows have no Change links: the whole address is changed through the Edit button.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS view page has no type row and no Change links (repo-insfrontend-p2-040, repo-insfrontend-p2-050).

requirements.statement: The view page's 'Edit' button, to /address-book/{id}/edit, is a secondary button, beside the Delete button in a button group.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 styles Edit as secondary.
requirements.deltaNote: Today Edit is a primary (green) button-link to /address-book/{id}/edit (repo-insfrontend-p2-051).

requirements.statement: The view page has a red warning 'Delete' button to /address-book/{id}/delete.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS view page has a warning 'Delete' button-link (repo-insfrontend-p2-052, trace-ins-fit-p2-045).

requirements.statement: With no return path, the view page's Back link goes to the address book list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS view page's Back link goes to /address-book (repo-insfrontend-p2-039, trace-ins-fit-p2-047).

requirements.statement: The view and delete pages honour a return query: the view page's Back link goes to it, its Edit and Delete links carry it on, the delete page's Back and 'No, cancel' carry it to the view page, and after a delete the user goes to it unless it is one of the deleted address's own pages, when they go to the list. A return is honoured when it starts with a single / (an INS page), or when it is an absolute URL whose origin exactly equals the configured animals frontend origin, so a user who opened the address from a journey page of either animals set (live-animals or germinal-products, both in the animals frontend) goes back to it; anything else falls back to the list (view page) or the view page (delete page). The return parameter's name is the INS service's to choose, and the allow-list stays. Locally, on the compose stack and in CDP the allowed origin is each environment's animals frontend base URL; in the INS stub mode only same-origin paths are honoured.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sends the user back to where they opened the address from; the animals frontend is on another origin, a cross-service constraint that extends the prototype's single-/ rule to that one origin and never to any origin (c-170).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the view page's Back always goes to the list and a delete always lands on the list (repo-insfrontend-p2-039, repo-insfrontend-p2-061).

requirements.statement: Opening the view page for an id that is not a live address in the organisation's book (unknown, malformed, another organisation's or deleted) sends the user to the view page's back link (the return path or the list) rather than a 404 page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 redirects a dead address link instead of showing an error.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a malformed id, an unknown or other organisation's id and a deleted address all respond 404 Page not found (repo-insfrontend-p2-033, repo-insfrontend-p2-035, repo-insfrontend-p2-036).

requirements.statement: Opening the delete page for an id that is not a live address in the book redirects to the return path or the list; posting a delete for such an id changes nothing, shows no banner and redirects as a delete would.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 treats a stale delete as a no-op rather than an error.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the delete page and its POST respond 404 when the address is missing or deleted (repo-insfrontend-p2-061, repo-insfrontend-p2-062).

requirements.statement: The address view page showing addresses found outside the book (a notification's consignment, contact or transporter addresses), without Edit or Delete.
requirements.why: Set aside by c-173: those addresses are copies held by the notification service, not the address book, so the INS view page reads the book only.

requirements.statement: When the address book service fails unexpectedly, the list renders the shared recoverable error banner with no table, and the view and delete pages respond with the service error page; each failure is logged.
requirements.why: A real cross-service failure the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS list renders 'There is a problem' on failure and the view and delete pages respond 500 (repo-insfrontend-p2-025, repo-insfrontend-p2-037, repo-insfrontend-p2-062).

requirements.statement: The list renders in the wide display column; the view and delete pages in the two-thirds column; every page keeps the skip link and the standard GOV.UK footer.
requirements.why: Today's layout; nothing in Design Release 2.1 changes it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p2-027 and repo-insfrontend-p2-038-m1 set the columns; trace-ins-fit-p2-002-m1 shows the footer.

requirements.statement: The list, view and delete pages have no serious or critical axe violations against WCAG 2.0 A/AA, 2.1 A/AA and 2.2 AA after the changes.
requirements.why: Accessibility is a legal requirement for the service.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS fit suite runs axe on each page and passes today (repo-insfrontend-p2-085, repo-insfrontend-p2-092, repo-insfrontend-p2-096).

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation is served by GET and POST at /address-book/{id}/delete.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree; Design Release 2.1 overrides only this address book view.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS delete page is served at /address-book/{id}/delete by GET and POST (repo-insfrontend-p2-053).

requirements.statement: The delete page's heading is 'Delete this address?'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's heading.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the heading is 'Delete address' (repo-insfrontend-p2-054, trace-ins-fit-p3-046).

requirements.statement: The delete page shows a summary list with one row, 'Address', holding the name, each address line and the country on separate lines, leaving out any line that repeats one already shown (ignoring case) and never the email or phone; with none of those it shows 'Not applicable'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows what is being deleted before the user confirms.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the delete page shows only the address's name, in its question (repo-insfrontend-p2-056).

requirements.statement: Below the summary the delete page says 'Confirm that you want to delete this address.', in place of today's 'Are you sure you want to delete <name> from your address book?'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording; the name now shows in the summary.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page asks 'Are you sure you want to delete <name> from your address book?' with the name in bold (repo-insfrontend-p2-055, trace-ins-fit-p3-048).

requirements.statement: The delete page warns 'This action cannot be undone.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 warns the user; it is true, as the API has no restore.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's page has no such warning (repo-insfrontend-p2-055).

requirements.statement: The delete page's confirm button is a red warning button reading 'Yes, delete'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's button text.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the button reads 'Yes, delete this address' (repo-insfrontend-p2-059, trace-ins-fit-p3-050).

requirements.statement: Beside the confirm button the delete page has a 'No, cancel' link to the address's view page, deleting nothing and showing no banner.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 offers cancel as a link, not a second button.

requirements.why: A test-coverage gap in a contract this programme does not change; it goes to the report.

requirements.statement: Adding and editing an address happen in the INS front door (trade-imports-ins-frontend) for a signed-in user, saved to the address-book service and scoped to the user's organisation: every address-book call carries the organisation id in the path and the Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header, an address is only ever found inside that organisation, and a submit without an organisation on the session is refused.
requirements.why: The address book moved out of the animals frontend to the INS front door, and organisation scoping is the only guard on whose addresses a user sees.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-002, p3-039, p3-072 and repo-addressbook-p2-094 already serve add and edit from the INS front door, signed in and organisation-scoped.

requirements.statement: Adding an address starts on a new 'Choose an address type' page, before any address fields, with a 'Back' link to the address book list. The type step takes a path of its own in the INS front door's path shape; the address form stays at /address-book/add.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks what kind of address is being added first, because that decides the form and the uses offered next.

requirements.statement: The add remembers the chosen address type between its steps, so coming back to 'Choose an address type' pre-selects it; opening the add afresh, and saving, clear the type, the entered address, the ticked uses and the search, so the next add starts empty.

requirements.deltaNote: Today the add is one page that always opens blank (repo-insfrontend-p3-033); there is no in-progress state to keep or clear.

requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 adds transporters through their own pages, not the address form; the address book record has no transporter category. Which service owns transporter records, and where their pages live, follow the real services (ruling 9 October, claim 21).
requirements.blockedBy: It is decided whether the service manages transporters at all and, if so, whether the address book or something else does; ruling 9 October pm (point 2) blocks transporter management pending those requirements and names nobody to decide, and the transporter area is re-distilled once it is decided.

requirements.statement: Once address search is built, and only if design keeps it under design question 10, 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' and 'Branch' open the add-details step with only the address search; the address fields, contact fields and uses question stay hidden until an address is picked or manual entry is chosen, and open already revealed when an address or address line 1 is already present.

requirements.blockedBy: Design answers design question 10 (address search: whether the GOV.UK address pattern with the fields always visible will do) in the waiting-on-design theme, and the address lookup becomes a real feature of the INS front door and INS backend (today only the EUDPA-390 spike exists, gated to dev and local and not wired in); this JavaScript addition is one waiting-on-design increment, also blocked on the lookup (ruling 9 October pm, claims p1-086 and p1-087), and the address search area is re-distilled once both land.

requirements.statement: Once address search is built, and only if design keeps it under design question 10, typing in the address search shows matches as the user types (a free-text type-ahead, not a postcode-then-pick step): matching addresses appear below the field in a list labelled 'Address search results', each shown as 'name, address, country' with the typed text in bold, and a screen-reader announcement gives the number of results (for example '1 result available').
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 search behaviour. Search as the user types needs JavaScript that no accepted component gives, so it waits on design; the search that works without JavaScript is req-2043.
requirements.blockedBy: Design answers design question 10 (address search: whether the GOV.UK address pattern with the fields always visible will do) in the waiting-on-design theme, and the address lookup becomes a real feature of the INS front door and INS backend (today only the EUDPA-390 spike exists, gated to dev and local and not wired in); this JavaScript addition is one waiting-on-design increment, also blocked on the lookup (ruling 9 October pm, claims p1-086 and p1-087), and the address search area is re-distilled once both land.

requirements.statement: Once address search is built, picking a search result fills address line 1, address line 2, town or city and postcode from the result (composed as c-178 sets out), with country United Kingdom; email address and phone number stay blank for the user, and any field the user types over wins.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 fills the address from the pick and leaves the contact details to the user. Hiding the search, revealing the fields and the 'Selected <name>' announcement on a pick are JavaScript additions that wait on design (req-2044).

requirements.blockedBy: The address lookup becomes a real feature of the INS front door and INS backend (today only the EUDPA-390 spike exists, gated to dev and local on a standalone page and not wired in); once it lands, the address search area is re-distilled (ruling 9 October, claim 34).

requirements.statement: Once the address lookup is a real feature, the address searches find real UK addresses from the address lookup the INS backend serves (find=<term>, carrying the trace id), and a failed lookup leaves the user able to enter the address manually. Which environments it runs in, and what else search needs, are settled when this area is re-distilled after the lookup lands.
requirements.why: The prototype's search list is made-up data shipped with the page; the real service must search real addresses, which only the address lookup holds (c-178). Sam ruled the search waits for the lookup to become a real feature (c-217).

requirements.statement: Add and edit keep today's length limits and email format check, in the frontend and the address book API: name and both address lines 255 characters, town or city and county 100, postcode 12, phone 20 and email 254, each with its '<field> must be N characters or fewer' message, and 'Enter an email address in the correct format' for a malformed email; postcode and phone stay free text.

requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows the user the address they just added among its kind.
requirements.deltaNote: Today saving returns to the unfiltered list at /address-book (repo-insfrontend-p3-076, trace-ins-fit-p1-054).

requirements.statement: After adding an address the list shows a 'Success' notification banner reading '<name> address added to your address book', where <name> is the name saved on the new address.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy. The prototype also has a nameless fallback, 'Address added to your address book', but it is not built: the add form and the address book API both require a name, so a save without one never reaches the list and the fallback can never show.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the banner reads '<name> added to your address book' (repo-insfrontend-p3-077, trace-ins-fit-p1-056).

requirements.statement: An added or edited address reads as address line 1, address line 2, town or city, county and postcode joined by commas, leaving out blanks, with the country shown separately.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's formatted address keeps every line the user gave.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the list's Address column shows only address line 1, town or city and postcode (trace-ins-fit-p1-058).

requirements.statement: A saved address can be found by the address book search on its name, its uses, its address and its country.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 makes the uses searchable along with the address.

requirements.statement: Creating an address persists its full record in the address-book service: POST /organisation/{orgId}/addresses answers 201 with a Location header ending in the new id, the address starts ACTIVE (deleted false) with server-set id, organisation and timestamps, and server-owned or unknown fields in the body are ignored.
requirements.why: The prototype keeps addresses only in the session; the real service must persist them.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p2-006 and repo-tests-p5-094 show a created address persisted with its full record.

requirements.statement: Saving an edit fully replaces the address's editable fields through PUT /organisation/{orgId}/addresses/{id}: a cleared optional field is cleared, id, organisation, status, createdAt and expiry are kept, modifiedAt moves on, and the record stays live.
requirements.why: An edit must change the stored address in place, not add a new one.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p2-039 and repo-tests-p5-104 show an edit replacing the record in place.

requirements.statement: An update is refused without change when the body is invalid (400 with per-field errors), the id is unknown, another organisation's or deleted (404 'Address not found'), or another write changed the address first (409 conflict); a stale write can never bring a deleted address back.
requirements.why: Persistence and authorisation constraints the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p2-044 to p2-052 prove these refusals.

requirements.statement: The address-book API answers errors as RFC 9457 problems (application/problem+json, CDP problem types, traceId from x-cdp-request-id, no instance field): a validation error carries a camelCase per-field errors map, a bad request carries none, a 500 never leaks the underlying message.
requirements.why: The frontend maps these shapes to the form, and the shapes are a locked cross-service contract.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p2-073 to p2-092 define and test these problem shapes.

requirements.statement: When the address-book service rejects a save the form is shown again with the service's first message per field and the values kept; any other save failure, or a failure loading the form, shows the recoverable error with the values kept; reference data being unavailable or empty gives a 503.
requirements.why: Cross-service failures the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-026 to p3-029 and p3-068 to p3-069 already handle these failures.

requirements.statement: Outside prod, a new address can be given an expiry (ADDRESS_TTL_DAYS) after which Mongo removes it; updates and deletes keep the original expiry, and prod is protected by two safeguards and keeps addresses indefinitely.
requirements.why: Test data must not build up outside prod while prod data is never expired.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p1-069 to p1-082 and p2-027 to p2-030 implement and test the non-prod expiry.

requirements.statement: The address-book service keeps its API surface and storage as built: the response fields (with deleted derived from status, and status, version and expireAt never returned), camelCase wire names, the hand-authored locked contract checked at build, the org_status_created index, Mongo over TLS with IAM in CDP, operation timers, and integration tests against a real Mongo.
requirements.why: This is the system of record other services depend on; none of it differs from Design Release 2.1 visibly.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p1-045 to p1-068 and p2-067 to p2-102 describe the service as built.

requirements.statement: The edit page's heading and page title are 'Edit address and contact details', with no caption.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the edit heading and title are 'Edit address details' (repo-insfrontend-p3-083, trace-ins-fit-p3-002).

requirements.statement: The edit page at /address-book/{id}/edit opens with the address and contact fields shown and prefilled from the stored address, with no address search.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-085 and trace-ins-fit-p3-006 show every field prefilled.

requirements.statement: The edit page's 'Back' link goes to the return path it was opened with, otherwise to the address's view page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 returns the user to where they came from.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the Back link always goes to the view page and the edit page carries no return context at all (repo-insfrontend-p3-084, p3-094).

requirements.statement: The edit page's buttons are 'Save changes' and a secondary 'Cancel', both submit buttons.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy, already met.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-089 and trace-ins-fit-p3-019 show 'Save changes' and a secondary submit 'Cancel'.

requirements.statement: 'Cancel' on the edit page saves nothing, clears any errors and returns to the return path, by default the address's view page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sends the user back to the address they were looking at.
requirements.deltaNote: Today Cancel goes to the address book list at /address-book (repo-insfrontend-p3-090, trace-ins-fit-p3-039).

requirements.statement: The edit page does not show or change the address's uses: an edit keeps every use the address already has.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps the type off the edit form; the record must not lose uses on edit.

requirements.statement: A valid edit returns the user to the address book list (its default view), which shows the edited values under the same address.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree on the destination; the list must show what was saved.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-092 and trace-ins-fit-p3-034, p3-037 show the return to /address-book with the edited values.

requirements.statement: After a valid edit the list shows a 'Success' notification banner reading '<Name> address updated', the name with its first letter capitalised and the rest lower case.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy, asserted by its specs and traces. The prototype also has a blank-name fallback, 'Address updated', but it is not built: the edit form and the address book API both require a name, so no valid edit has a blank one and the fallback can never show.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the banner reads '<name> updated in your address book' with the name as typed (repo-insfrontend-p3-092, trace-ins-fit-p3-035).

requirements.statement: Opening or saving the edit page for an address that is not in the user's address book (unknown, another organisation's, deleted or a malformed id) redirects to the return path or the address book list without saving.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sends the user back to the list rather than an error page.
requirements.deltaNote: Today these cases show the page not found error (repo-insfrontend-p3-080, p3-081, p3-093).
