requirements.statement: Every new or changed English string on the add and edit pages gets a matching Welsh entry, still marked as an unreviewed machine draft that must not ship without Welsh Language Standards sign-off.
requirements.why: The address book keeps English and Welsh copy side by side; changing only English would leave Welsh describing the old pages.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's Welsh copy mirrors today's English (repo-insfrontend-p3-114 to p3-120).

requirements.statement: Every add and edit page highlights 'Address book' in the service navigation.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-ins-fit-p1-007 and p3-021 show 'Address book' active.

requirements.statement: The add and edit pages, and their error states, use only GOV.UK Frontend components and have no serious or critical axe violations against WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 A and AA.
requirements.why: Accessibility is a standing quality bar the new pages must keep.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-124 to p3-135 and trace-ins-fit-p1-027, p3-043 show no serious or critical violations.

requirements.statement: The add and edit forms post to themselves with browser validation off and a CSRF crumb, set autocomplete only on email, and are served with the INS security headers and session cookie; the add page is sent with Cache-Control: no-store.
requirements.why: Security and form handling constraints the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-020, p3-031 and trace-ins-fit-p1-025, p1-054-m1 show these protections.

requirements.statement: The edit page is sent without Cache-Control: no-store, unlike the add page, so a browser may cache a page holding an organisation's address and contact details.
requirements.why: Not a Design Release 2.1 difference: a gap in today's service that this programme does not fix; it goes to the report.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-032.

requirements.statement: A notification journey's 'Add a new address' keeps handing over to the INS address book add through today's handshake (journey-type, notification-id, fulfilment-id and handshake-token; only the registered gbn-ag journey; the return URL built on the server; the new address id handed back; cancel returns without one; no address book banner). In journey mode the INS add page shows Design Release 2.1's add-address page, skips 'Choose an address type', opens the 'Add address and contact details' step for the type the role implies with the role's use ticked, and returns through the journey's /address-return to the page each button names: 'Save and select' commits the copy and lands on the Consignment addresses page, 'Save and return to address page' lands on the picker unselected, and 'Cancel and return to hub' saves nothing. The same holds on the compose stack and in CDP.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's journeys add addresses on their own pages, but which service writes the address book is cross-service behaviour the prototype cannot express, so the real address book stays a separate service reached through this handshake while everything the prototype can express about the page follows Design Release 2.1 (c-106).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the handshake opens the single 'Add address details' form with 'Cancel and return to address page' (repo-insfrontend-p3-107, p3-108).

requirements.statement: Once address search is built with the search-only layout (design question 10), when that layout ('Destination, Consignee or Importer', 'Branch') is saved with nothing picked or typed, the six field errors show and the address and contact fields are revealed, so each error summary link leads to a visible field; errors stay on the fields until the next save, and what was typed, the ticked uses and the search text are kept.
requirements.why: An error summary link must reach its field; the prototype's hidden fields are a gap, not a design choice.
requirements.blockedBy: Design answers design question 10 (address search: whether the GOV.UK address pattern with the fields always visible will do) in the waiting-on-design theme, and the address lookup becomes a real feature of the INS front door and INS backend (today only the EUDPA-390 spike exists, gated to dev and local and not wired in); this JavaScript addition is one waiting-on-design increment, also blocked on the lookup (ruling 9 October pm, claims p1-086 and p1-087), and the address search area is re-distilled once both land.

requirements.statement: No separate 'What can this address be used for?' usage page (/address-book/add/usage, with a hint on each use and a 'Save address' button) is built; the uses are asked on the add-details step.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 holds this page but never reaches it: it redirects unless a pending address is held, and nothing sets one.

requirements.statement: The prototype's root 'Add address details' lookup page (full UK and EU search list, County field, 'Cancel and return to dashboard', single suggested type, no uses question) is not built as a separate page.
requirements.why: Under Design Release 2.1 it is reached only by the non-DR2.1 journey hand-off; the address book's own add uses the 'Add address and contact details' step.

requirements.statement: Design Release 1's seven address types (Place of Origin to Branch Address with their hints), its 'What is the new address for?' chooser and its add-details form are not built.
requirements.why: The DR1 parity backlog is not a source of requirements; Design Release 2.1's four types and their uses replace DR1's add journey.

requirements.statement: The dev/local-only address lookup spike page (/address-lookup-spike, EUDPA-390) is left as it is: its search form, outcome tags, timings, mapping summary, stub and Welsh draft copy are not changed to match Design Release 2.1.
requirements.why: It is a temporary engineering spike users never reach, not part of any Design Release 2.1 page; the real search reuses its lookup client (req-1218).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p5-003: registered in dev and local only.

requirements.statement: The INS frontend's shared validators (UK postcode format, vehicle registration, UK phone, number ranges, dates and times) stay unused by the address form.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sets no format rule on postcode or phone, the germinal data fields define none, and today's form uses none of these validators; nothing changes while c-256 keeps phone free text.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-121.

requirements.statement: The service has a Manage templates page, served by the animals frontend, with the page title 'Manage templates - Import notification service - GOV.UK' and the H1 'Manage templates'; its path follows the animals frontend's conventions.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives users one place to find, use and create notification templates; no real service has templates today. Templates are create, read, update and delete work that goes ahead now (ruling of 9 October on templates). The ruling does not say which frontend serves the page; the animals frontend does, because the animals backend stores templates (req-1310) and template mode walks the animals sets' own journey pages, and the other frontends' Templates navigation items link across to it.

requirements.statement: Under the Manage templates heading the page shows the line 'Select, manage or create new notification templates'.
requirements.why: The design's introductory copy for the templates list.

requirements.statement: Manage templates has a primary 'Create new template' button (a link styled as a button) that starts a new template.
requirements.why: The design's way into creating a template.

requirements.statement: Every templates page (Manage templates, Enter template name, the template page, and the delete and discard confirmations) shows the Alpha phase banner 'This is a new service. Help us improve it and give your feedback by email.', the feedback link going to the service's real feedback address rather than the prototype's '#'.
requirements.why: The design shows the phase banner on every templates page; the prototype's dead '#' link is a placeholder.

requirements.statement: On every templates page the service navigation marks 'Templates' as the active item.
requirements.why: Templates is a top-level area of the service in the design, beside the dashboard and address book.

requirements.statement: Manage templates has no Back link: it starts directly with its heading.
requirements.why: It is a top-level page reached from the service navigation or from the 'Use template' button on a dashboard, which opens it.

requirements.statement: The templates are listed under an H2 'My templates'.
requirements.why: The design's heading for the list.

requirements.statement: Above the template cards a results count reads 'Show 1-N of N results' for N templates, or 'Show 0 of 0 results' with none; every template is listed on one page with no pagination control.
requirements.why: The design's results count; it shows no paging.

requirements.statement: Manage templates gets a sort control only as design answers design question 11 (templates sort): either a GET form whose button really reorders the list, with the options design names, or nothing, in which case this requirement is dropped. Design Release 2.1's inert 'Sort by:' select (Select one, Newest first, Oldest first, Arrival date, outside any form and reordering nothing) is not built.
requirements.why: A control that does nothing is not shipped, and 'Arrival date' has no meaning for templates, which hold no arrival date; the 9 October afternoon ruling moves the whole sort row to the waiting-on-design theme and replaces c-185's inert select (c-185).
requirements.blockedBy: Design answers design question 11 (templates sort) in the waiting-on-design theme: a sort that really reorders, with the options design names, or no sort at all.

requirements.statement: Manage templates has no filter, no search and no 'Sort by' control, and no empty-state message: with no templates it shows the results count and an empty list.
requirements.why: The design has no filter, search or empty-state message, and shows only the count when the list is empty; its inert sort select is not shipped while design question 11 is open (req-1299, c-185).

requirements.statement: The templates list shows the user's saved templates newest saved first, leaving out any template that has been deleted.
requirements.why: The design's list order: a template just saved appears at the top.

requirements.statement: Each template is a card labelled 'Template <title>' that shows the template's category label above the template title, which is an H3.
requirements.why: The design's template card.

requirements.statement: Each template card has a 'View template' link to that template's page and a 'Use template' control that starts a notification from it in the template's own set (live animals or germinal products). 'Use template' is a GOV.UK secondary button in a form that posts, beside 'View template', keeping the design's wording.
requirements.why: The card's two actions in the design; templates carry their type, so each card starts a notification in its own set (ruling 9 October). Using a template stores a new draft, and every state change is a form post protected against request forgery, so the design's link becomes a GOV.UK button (c-309).

requirements.statement: Each template card lists, in this order, Commodity (the commodity common names), Origin (the country of origin), Consignee (the consignee's name) and Consignor (the consignor's name), each reading 'Not applicable' when the template has no answer.
requirements.why: The design summarises a template by these four answers so a user can tell templates apart.

requirements.statement: A template's category label is the set it was created in: 'Live animals' for a live animals template and 'Germinal products' for a germinal products template.
requirements.why: The design labels each template card with its category; each set holds one category and a template carries its type, so the label comes from the type rather than from working out what the goods are (c-266).

requirements.statement: The templates pages render as the design does, built from GOV.UK Frontend components (summary cards for the template card and the answer cards, the standard caption, heading, input, button and button group) where the prototype wraps them in custom app-dr2-* and app-view-template-page blocks.
requirements.why: The prototype's custom blocks are its own scaffolding; the real services stay inside the GOV.UK Frontend toolbox while matching what users see.

requirements.statement: A success message on Manage templates shows as a GOV.UK success notification banner (role alert) titled 'Success' with the message as its heading, shown once; it does not dismiss itself and stays until the trader leaves or reloads the page.
requirements.why: The design confirms saves and deletions this way; its 5-second auto-dismiss gives way to the accessibility duty (c-006), and the 9 October afternoon ruling keeps success banners on screen because WCAG 2.2.1 rules out a message that leaves on a timer.

requirements.statement: Saving a template shows the banner '<template title> saved to templates' on Manage templates.
requirements.why: The design's confirmation that the template was saved.

requirements.statement: Deleting a template shows the banner '<template title> has been deleted' on Manage templates.
requirements.why: The design's confirmation that the template was deleted.

requirements.statement: Templates are stored by the animals backend and kept between sessions: a user's list holds only templates really saved, with no seeded example templates.
requirements.why: The prototype keeps templates in the browser session with five seeded examples because it cannot persist; persistence is a real constraint that overrides the prototype (c-183, kept by the 9 October ruling). Template mode offers only the types whose service stores templates, live animals and germinal products, both in the animals services.

requirements.statement: A saved template is private to the signed-in user who saved it and is listed under their 'My templates'; nobody else sees, uses, changes or deletes it. How the store keys it is the backend's design.
requirements.why: The prototype keeps saved templates to the user who made them under 'My templates'; real persistence and sign-in only replace its session with a store scoped to that user (c-184). The data shape is not the prototype's to decide.

requirements.statement: Opening, changing, using or deleting a template that does not exist, has been deleted or belongs to another user redirects to Manage templates.
requirements.why: The design never shows an error page for a missing template.

requirements.statement: 'Create new template' starts a new, empty template and sends the user to the notification type question first; the journey then runs notification type, Enter template name, then the notification questions from Origin of the import. Following the 'Create new template' link stores nothing: the template is first stored by a form post in that journey. Any draft notification the user already has is left untouched.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks the type before the name so the template's questions fit its type. The prototype clears its one in-session journey; real drafts are persisted, so starting a template leaves them alone (c-183). A link never changes stored state (c-309).

requirements.statement: In template creation the notification type page asks 'What are you importing?' under the caption 'About the consignment', with radios offering only Live animals and Germinal products (semen, ova, embryos), none preselected, and a 'Continue' button that leads to the template name page; its back link goes to Manage templates and it shows no 'Template' caption yet. Submitting it with no choice shows the page's usual error, whose error summary link goes to the first radio. The field name is the service's. Plants for planting, Potatoes (seed and ware) and Wood products are left out until the plants service has templates.
requirements.why: The design's first step of a new template. Template mode offers only the types whose service stores templates, so the plants types are left out until plants has templates (c-265); the field name is not the prototype's to decide.

requirements.statement: The template name page has the caption 'Create a new template', the H1 'Enter template name' and the page title 'Enter template name - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
requirements.why: The design's template name page.

requirements.statement: The template name page has one text input, labelled by the H1 with a visually hidden label 'Enter template name', and no hint. The field name is the service's.
requirements.why: The design's single question on the page.

requirements.statement: The template name is optional and unvalidated: the form posts with browser validation off, and a blank name moves on to Origin of the import with no error; there is no length, character or duplicate-name rule.
requirements.why: The design accepts any name, including none.

requirements.statement: A template saved with no name is titled 'Untitled template': the banner reads 'Untitled template saved to templates' and it is listed first with every card field 'Not applicable' when nothing was answered.
requirements.why: The design's fallback name for an unnamed template.

requirements.statement: The template name page has a 'Save and continue' button and a 'Cancel and return to manage templates' link to Manage templates.
requirements.why: The design's actions on the name page.

requirements.statement: The template name page's back link goes to the notification type page when a type has been chosen, and to Manage templates otherwise.
requirements.why: The design's back navigation from the name page.

requirements.statement: The template name field is prefilled with the name already entered only while the user is part way through creating that template, and is otherwise empty; a saved template's name cannot be changed afterwards.
requirements.why: The design sets the name only at creation and offers no rename.

requirements.statement: Submitting the template name trims it and opens Origin of the import for the new template, keeping the chosen notification type.
requirements.why: The design's hand-off from the name page into the template's questions.

requirements.statement: A template is answered on the same question pages as a notification, with the same questions, hints and guidance (for example the origin page's country search, region of origin and internal reference, and the commodity page's ITAHC guidance and trade tariff link), each page in template mode showing a 'Template' caption with the template name above the section caption.
requirements.why: The design reuses the notification questions for templates and marks them as a template.

requirements.statement: While a new template is being created, Origin of the import shows the 'Template' caption and name and the caption 'About the consignment', offers only 'Save and continue' (no Cancel link), and its back link returns to the template name page.
requirements.why: The design's first question page in template creation.

requirements.statement: While a new template is being created, 'What are you importing?' shows the 'Template' caption and name, has a back link to the origin page, and offers 'Save and continue', 'Save and return to overview' and a 'Cancel and return to overview' link to the template's task list.
requirements.why: The design's commodity page actions in template creation.

requirements.statement: In template mode, saving 'What are you importing?' returns to the template's task list instead of going on to the main import reason.
requirements.why: The design lets the user choose which template sections to fill from the task list.

requirements.statement: While a template is being created, the status strip on its task list and question pages shows a grey 'Template' tag followed by the template's name, in place of the draft status and notification reference.
requirements.why: The design marks the task list as a template's.

requirements.statement: A template's task list is headed 'Template tasklist' instead of 'Notification tasklist', and keeps the 'Overview' H1 and the 'Your commodities' figures for animals and packages (0 and 0 before any are entered).
requirements.why: The design's template task list heading and overview.

requirements.statement: A template's task list has five sections and no Documents section or 'Upload documents' task: '1. About the consignment', '2. Description of the goods', '3. Transport and arrival', '4. Consignment parties' and '5. Contact address'.
requirements.why: Documents are specific to one consignment, so the design leaves them out of templates.

requirements.statement: A live animals template's tasks are: Where is this consignment coming from?, What are you importing?, Main import reason, Commodity details, Identification details, Additional details, Arrival details, Transport details, Roles and addresses (hint 'Consignor or Exporter, Consignee, Importer and Place of Destination') and Contact address for this consignment, each linking to its question page.
requirements.why: The design's template task list. No ?from= marker is copied; the pages' return behaviour is the service's (ruling 9 October).

requirements.statement: Each task on a template's task list shows a status tag: green 'Complete' when answered, blue 'To do' otherwise.
requirements.why: The design shows the user which template sections are filled.

requirements.statement: A template's task list ends with a primary 'Review template' button to the template review ('Review your template') and a secondary 'Return to manage templates' button to Manage templates, in place of 'Review and submit' and 'Return to dashboard'.
requirements.why: The design's template task list actions.

requirements.statement: A template never offers documents or a declaration: nothing on a template's task list, pages or review leads to Upload documents or the declaration, and the template review's main button saves the template instead. The prototype's redirects that guard the documents, declaration and submitted addresses in template mode are not required.
requirements.why: A template has no documents and no declaration (ruling 9 October); the prototype's URL guards are its own routing and are not required (c-264).

requirements.statement: The template review's back link returns to the template's task list.
requirements.why: The design's back navigation from the template review.

requirements.statement: While a template is being created, the template review's Change links open each question page directly to change the template in progress, not the saved-template change flow (with its 'Save and return' and 'Cancel' back to the template page).
requirements.why: During creation the template is still a draft being reviewed.

requirements.statement: 'Save template' saves the template, even with only some sections answered, and returns to Manage templates with the new template first in the list and the count one higher.
requirements.why: The design lets a user save a partial template.

requirements.statement: Saving a template that is being edited overwrites it, keeping its id, and moves it to the top of the list rather than adding a copy.
requirements.why: Dropped by the 9 October ruling with the unlinked whole-template edit mode (c-261): no page links to that mode, so saving a template being edited through it is not built. A saved template is changed one section at a time (req-1361).

requirements.statement: A new template's id, used in its addresses, is its title in lower case with every run of other characters replaced by a hyphen ('template' if nothing is left), with -2, -3 and on added when the user already has that id.
requirements.why: Dropped by the 9 October ruling: template ids built from titles are data-model shape copied from the prototype (c-259). How a template is identified is the backend's design.

requirements.statement: A template's date created is set to the day it is saved, and is reset each time it is saved again after a change.
requirements.why: The design shows this date on the template page and updates it on every save.

requirements.statement: A template saves the notification's country and region of origin, internal reference, commodity codes, common names and species, reason for import, purpose in the market, certified for, unweaned animals, storage temperature, animal and package totals and per-species numbers, commodity selections, net weight, package type, animal identification details, port of entry, means of transport, transport identification, transport document reference, the transporter's name, address, country, approval number and type, and the CPH number.
requirements.why: These are the answers the design carries from one consignment to the next.

requirements.statement: A template never holds an arrival date or time, including after a section of an existing template is changed and saved.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 leaves the arrival date out of templates because it differs for every consignment. The templates ruling's hedged 'maybe the same data' does not change which questions a template asks (c-318's default).

requirements.statement: A template saves the place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer, place of destination and contact address each as answered, shows them on the template page's Addresses card (Place of origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer, Place of destination) and Contact address card as the design renders them, and seeds each back into a notification started from it; the contact address falls back to the place of origin where none was chosen, as the design does.
requirements.why: The real notification persists the parties separately and sends each downstream as its own party, so the prototype's shortcut of copying the place of origin into every party would name the overseas place of origin as the GB consignee, importer and destination: a cross-service constraint the prototype cannot express (c-186).

requirements.statement: A saved template's page has the caption 'Templates' above the template's title, which is its H1 and its page title ('<template name> - Import notification service - GOV.UK').
requirements.why: The design's page for one saved template.

requirements.statement: The template page shows 'Date created: <d Month yyyy>' with the template's date created.
requirements.why: The design shows when the template was last saved.

requirements.statement: The template page has a primary 'Use template' button, a submit button in a form that posts, which starts a notification from the template, and a red warning 'Delete' button that opens the template's delete confirmation.
requirements.why: The design's actions on a saved template. Using a template stores a new draft, so its button posts instead of being a link styled as a button; it looks the same (c-309).

requirements.statement: The template page's back link goes to Manage templates.
requirements.why: The design's back navigation from a template.

requirements.statement: The template page has no Edit button or link, and there is no whole-template edit: a saved template is changed one section at a time through its Change links.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows no edit action on the template page, and the 9 October ruling drops its unlinked edit mode (c-261).

requirements.statement: The template page lists the template's answers in the same cards as the notification review, in five numbered sections, '1. About the consignment' (Origin of import, What are you importing?, Main import reason), '2. Description of the goods' (a card per commodity '<common name> (<code>)' with species, Number of animals, Number of packages (when required), the identification details table, and an Additional details card), '3. Transport and arrival' (Arrival details and Transport details), '4. Consignment addresses' and '5. Contact address', with no documents section and a Change link on every card.
requirements.why: The design lets the user check everything a template holds before using it.

requirements.statement: On the template page each card's Change link changes that section of the saved template: origin of the import, what you are importing, reason for import, consignment details (card header and number-of-animals row), animal identification details, additional animal details, arrival details, transporter, roles and addresses and contact address.
requirements.why: The design changes one section of a saved template at a time.

requirements.statement: A success message on the template page shows as a success banner titled 'Success', shown once and staying until the trader leaves or reloads the page; opening the template page abandons any half-finished change to a template.
requirements.why: The design's confirmation of a change, and its way of leaving an unfinished change; its 5-second auto-dismiss gives way to the accessibility duty (c-006).

requirements.statement: Posting to a template's page (/templates/<id>) changes nothing and redirects back to that page.
requirements.why: Dropped by the 9 October ruling: a POST to the template page is the prototype's routing, not look and feel (c-262).

requirements.statement: Following a template's Change link opens that section's question page prefilled from the template, to change the saved template rather than a notification; following the link stores nothing until the page is saved.
requirements.why: The design changes a saved template on the ordinary question pages.

requirements.statement: A Change address for a section that is not one of the template's sections redirects back to the template page.
requirements.why: Dropped by the 9 October ruling (claim 20, 'the section allow-list'; claim 21, template URL guards not required): a Change address for a section the template does not have is routing, not look and feel (c-263). The template page only links to the sections it shows.

requirements.statement: When changing a template section from its page or review, each journey page's only submit button is 'Save and return', beside a 'Cancel' link back to that template's page; this ending takes precedence over the amend ending.
requirements.why: The design's actions when changing one section of a saved template.

requirements.statement: When changing a template section, the question page's back link returns to the template page.
requirements.why: The design's back navigation when changing a template.

requirements.statement: When changing a template section, the question page is prefilled with the template's answers and can be edited; an unanswered optional field is empty, 'Not applicable' being only how the template page shows it.
requirements.why: The design edits the template's existing answers.

requirements.statement: Saving a changed template section saves the template, never a draft notification, and returns to the template's page, which shows the new answer and a success banner headed '<template name> has been updated' ('Template has been updated' when the template has no name); this holds for every section, not only the origin section the traces follow.
requirements.why: The design's confirmation that a template change was saved.

requirements.statement: Opening /templates/<id>/edit starts a draft seeded from the template in template-creation mode and opens the template's task list.
requirements.why: Dropped by the 9 October ruling: no page links to the whole-template edit mode, so it is not built (c-261).

requirements.statement: Using a template, by its 'Use template' form post, creates and saves a new draft notification in the template's own set, seeded from the template, and opens its task list headed 'Notification tasklist' with the status 'Draft' and a new GBN-AG notification reference made the same way as for any new notification. Any other draft the user has is left untouched.
requirements.why: Using a template is the design's quick way to start a notification from saved answers. The prototype clears its one in-session journey; real drafts are persisted, so using a template leaves them alone (c-183). It stores a draft, so it is a form post, never a GET (c-309). Germinal notifications keep GBN-AG references.

requirements.statement: A notification started from a template uses its set's normal notification task list, including '4. Documents' and '5. Consignment parties', ending with 'Review and submit' and 'Return to dashboard', which goes to the set's own notification list; nothing on it says which template it came from.
requirements.why: Once started, it is an ordinary notification; the design does not show where it came from. Every page Design Release 2.1 sends to the overall dashboard goes to the set's own notification list instead (ruling of 9 October, afternoon).

requirements.statement: The overview of a notification started from a template shows the template's animal and package totals under 'Your commodities'.
requirements.why: The template's numbers carry over.

requirements.statement: A notification started from a template records the template's id and title, but nothing on its task list says which template it came from.
requirements.why: Dropped by the 9 October ruling: recording the template's id on the notification is data-model shape copied from the prototype, and nothing a user sees depends on it (c-260). req-1364 keeps that the task list does not name the template.

requirements.statement: Using a template seeds the country of origin, the region of origin ('Yes' with the code when the template has one, 'No' when it does not) and the internal reference (blank when the template has none).
requirements.why: The origin answers carry over.

requirements.statement: Using a template starts the notification in the template's own set, selects the template's commodities and species, and seeds the commodity selections, animal and package numbers per species, net weight, package type and animal identification details it holds.
requirements.why: The goods answers carry over; a template carries its type, so it starts a notification of that type (ruling 9 October).

requirements.statement: Using a live animals template seeds the main reason for import, the purpose in the internal market only when the reason is 'Internal market', 'certified for' when the template's value is a valid option (otherwise 'Further keeping'), and the unweaned animals answer when valid for the species ('No' when the species have unweaned options and the template has none).
requirements.why: The reason and additional details carry over, falling back to valid answers. The 9 October ruling splits this requirement per set; req-1875 carries the germinal half.

requirements.statement: Using a template seeds the CPH number, port of entry, means of transport, transport identification and transport document reference; it leaves the arrival date empty, so Arrival details and Upload documents show 'To do' on the new notification.
requirements.why: The transport answers carry over; the arrival date and documents are new for every consignment.

requirements.statement: Using a template seeds the transporter's name, address, approval number, type and country into the new notification.
requirements.why: The design saves and shows the transporter's country and, after a template is used, shows the same country again, worked out from the seeded approval number; the real service stores the country as an answer and a private transporter has no approval number, so it carries the saved country across to give the same result (c-187).

requirements.statement: Using a template seeds no documents and starts the notification with no validation errors.
requirements.why: Documents are never part of a template.

requirements.statement: A saved template's delete confirmation has the H1 'Delete this template?' and the page title 'Delete this template? - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
requirements.why: The design asks before a template is deleted.

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation shows a one-row summary list keyed 'Name' holding the template's title.
requirements.why: The design names the template being deleted.

requirements.statement: Under the summary the delete confirmation says 'Confirm that you want to delete this template.' and 'This action cannot be undone.'
requirements.why: The design's warning copy.

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation has a red warning 'Yes, delete' button that posts the deletion and a 'No, cancel' link back to the template page, in a GOV.UK button group.
requirements.why: The design's confirm and cancel actions.

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation's back link goes to the template page.
requirements.why: The design's back navigation from the delete confirmation.

requirements.statement: The delete and discard confirmations use the journey layout, not the dashboard layout.
requirements.why: The design renders the confirmation as a journey page.

requirements.statement: Confirming 'Yes, delete' removes the template and returns to Manage templates with the '<title> has been deleted' banner and one template fewer in the count.
requirements.why: The design's result of deleting a template.

requirements.statement: A template being created can be discarded from its review: a confirmation shows the same 'Delete this template?' page and copy, with the Name row holding the name entered ('this template' when none), a back link and 'No, cancel' link to the template review, and a 'Yes, delete' button that discards it.
requirements.why: The design lets a user throw away a template before saving it. The templates ruling lists discarding and deleting separately without saying how they differ; Design Release 2.1 settles it: discarding throws away a template not yet saved, deleting removes a saved one.

requirements.statement: The discard page is shown only while a template is being created; otherwise opening it redirects to Manage templates, and posting to it changes nothing and returns to Manage templates.
requirements.why: There is nothing to discard outside template creation.

requirements.statement: Confirming discard throws the template away unsaved and returns to Manage templates, list unchanged, with the banner '<template name> has been deleted', or 'Template has been deleted' when no name was entered.
requirements.why: The design's result of discarding a template.

requirements.statement: The prototype's /design-release-2.1 mount and its rule sending anyone not in a Design Release 2 or 2.1 session to the start page are not built; the real services serve the templates pages at their own paths behind their own sign-in.
requirements.why: Version mounting and design-release sessions are prototype mechanics, not part of the design.

requirements.statement: The 'Cancel' link on a template's change page pointing to /templates/<id> without the release prefix is not reproduced; Cancel goes to the template page.
requirements.why: A prototype path slip, not part of the design; req-1358 builds the working Cancel link.

requirements.statement: The prototype's unguarded discard post, which clears any notification in progress and shows a 'has been deleted' banner even when no template is being created, is not reproduced.
requirements.why: A prototype defect, not part of the design; req-1381 guards the post.

requirements.statement: The seeded Arena Aintree region code changing from 'ROI-092032' to 'IE-092032' on re-save is not a templates behaviour to build: it comes from seeded data no real service holds.
requirements.why: Seeded templates are not built (c-183); the region code form belongs to the origin page.

requirements.statement: The prototype's session-only storage and its five seeded templates (Arena Aintree, Rice Lane City Farm, Monk Park Farm, Acorn Farm and Glen Keen Farm, with their answers and the '15 April 2026' fallback date) are not built.
requirements.why: Persistence is a real constraint the prototype cannot express (c-183): real users see only templates they saved.

requirements.statement: Saving a template by a GET to /templates/save is not built: a template is saved only by the 'Save template' form post from the review page.
requirements.why: A state-changing GET bypasses the services' request forgery protection, a real constraint the prototype cannot express (c-188).

requirements.statement: 'Amend this notification' on a submitted notification's view page, and the Amend action on its card in the set's notification list, open an amend confirmation page at the notification's own amend route, in every set that amends (live animals, germinal products and plants): its title and level-1 heading are 'Amend notification', it asks 'Are you sure you want to change this notification?', and nothing changes until the trader confirms.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks the trader to confirm before reopening a submitted notification; the 9 October afternoon ruling keeps that confirmation as a page carrying the pop-up's wording, and puts every amendment, plants' included, behind it (c-190, c-310).
requirements.deltaNote: Today there is no amend confirmation: the card's Amend is a form button that starts the amendment straight away (trace-animals-fit-p3-027, trace-animals-fit-p3-028), as plants' card Amend does (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-115), and the view page offers no Amend (trace-e2e-p14-050).

requirements.statement: On the amend confirmation page, 'Yes, continue' is a button that submits the page's form (with the CSRF crumb) and starts the amendment, and 'No, go back' is a link-styled control that returns to the notification's view page without changing anything; the page's Back link goes to the view page too.
requirements.why: The trader confirms or backs out of amending without losing their place; a state change is a form post (c-189).

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, 'Amend this notification' and 'Cancel amend' open their confirmations as modal dialogs over the current page instead of going to the confirmation pages: hidden until opened, role dialog with aria-modal, labelled by the heading (the amend dialog also described by its question), each with a Close (X) button labelled 'Close' for screen readers and an overlay; Close, the overlay and the dialog's 'No, go back' or 'Go back' dismiss it without acting and leave the trader where they were. Built for live animals, germinal products and plants only if design makes a strong case; otherwise dropped.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 confirms in place. The 9 October afternoon ruling holds the pop-ups back: GOV.UK Frontend has no modal, MoJ's modal dialog is not accepted and has no fallback without JavaScript, and no custom JavaScript is written to copy the prototype (c-190).
requirements.blockedBy: Design answers design question 9 (the amend and cancel-amendment pop-ups) in the waiting-on-design theme; the expected answer is that they are not built, and the increment is then dropped.

requirements.statement: Confirming an amendment ('Yes, continue' on the amend confirmation page, reached from the view page or the card's Amend) takes the trader to the notification's review page (the amend review), not to its overview hub, in every set that amends: live animals, germinal products and plants (plants' own review page).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 opens an amendment on the review page so the trader sees every answer and its Change link at once; the 9 October afternoon ruling keeps this outcome and gives plants the same landing.
requirements.deltaNote: Today Amend posts to /notifications/{id}/amend and redirects to the overview hub showing 'Amending' (trace-animals-fit-p3-027, trace-e2e-p14-053, repo-tests-p4-098); the review page is one step further, behind Review and submit (trace-animals-fit-p3-031, repo-tests-p3-086). Plants takes the same landing on its own review page (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-043).

requirements.statement: Amending moves a SUBMITTED notification to AMEND, keeps its reference and original submitted time, stores a full independent snapshot of the submitted content and fulfilments, and records a NotificationAmendmentRequested event carrying the status history and the actor; an unknown reference gets 404 and any status but SUBMITTED gets 400.
requirements.why: The submitted version must survive the amendment so cancelling can restore it and other services see the change.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend amend endpoint already does this (repo-backend-p2-090, repo-backend-p2-094, repo-backend-p2-098), proven end to end (trace-e2e-p14-070).

requirements.statement: Answers changed during an amendment are saved to the notification record (status stays AMEND) as the trader goes, and are not visible as the submitted version until resubmitted.
requirements.why: The real service persists every save; the prototype's session-only amendment cannot express persistence.
requirements.deltaNote: Saving keeps a notification in AMEND (repo-backend-p2-111), and a changed value survives leaving the cancel page (trace-animals-fit-p3-042).

requirements.statement: A notification being amended shows the status tag 'Amend' in the shared status strip, changed once for every set (live animals, germinal products and plants).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names the state 'Amend'; the 9 October afternoon ruling changes the shared strip's label in every set at once.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the tag reads 'Amending' (yellow) on the hub, review and cancel pages (trace-animals-fit-p3-029, trace-e2e-p14-031).

requirements.statement: During an amendment, the review page and every question page show an Amend status bar above the caption and heading: the 'Amend' tag, the reference, and a link-styled 'Cancel amend' control that goes to the cancel-amendment confirmation page. It is a change to the shared status strip, so live animals, germinal products and plants all get it at once. Whether the hub's own status line carries it is req-782's.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader abandon the amendment from wherever they are in it; the 9 October afternoon ruling makes this the one change to the shared strip, and sends 'Cancel amend' to the confirmation page.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a 'Cancel amendment' link sits under the review page heading only; the hub and question pages offer no way to cancel (trace-animals-fit-p3-032, trace-animals-fit-p3-029-m1, trace-e2e-p14-055).

requirements.statement: The amend review has no page-header actions (no Amend this notification, no Copy as new), no Import reference numbers section and no Date submitted line.
requirements.why: During an amendment the status bar replaces the view page's header.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's amending view shows no Copy as new or Delete under its heading (trace-e2e-p14-032-m1) and has no Import reference numbers section or Date submitted line.

requirements.statement: The amend review is editable, with a Change link on every card (the first going to the origin of the import), and its Back link goes to the notification's overview hub.
requirements.why: Amending means changing the submitted answers.
requirements.deltaNote: The amending review already has Change links on every card and a Back link to the hub (trace-e2e-p14-032, trace-animals-fit-p3-034).

requirements.statement: While a submitted notification is being amended, each page the overview links to, including a question page opened from the amend review, ends with a primary 'Save and return' button that saves and goes to the amend review (which shows the changed answer), a secondary 'Save and continue' button that saves and goes to the next page, and a link-styled 'Save and return to overview' button, with no cancel link. The buttons post the real service's own fields (exit=hub and ?change=1 stay); no action=review|continue|hub field is added. The party pickers, the CPH number page and the permanent address page, which DR1 rule (b) keeps to the primary button outside amend, show 'Save and return' and 'Save and continue' only, without 'Save and return to overview'. Plants' save actions get the same three amend controls, and its pickers the same two buttons, in the same increment.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader return to the review straight after a change, or carry on.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a Change link opens the question with ?change=1 and saving returns to the notification view with no choice of where to go (trace-e2e-p14-047, repo-tests-p3-079).

requirements.statement: During an amendment, question pages keep the journey's usual Back links (the origin of the import back to the notification type page, arrival details back to the overview hub), not a link to the amend review.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 does not change Back links for an amendment.

requirements.statement: During an amendment, question pages are prefilled with the notification's saved answers and keep their usual copy (for example Arrival details: arrival date at port of entry with a d/m/yyyy date picker, port of entry search, means of transport, transport identification and document reference).
requirements.why: The trader changes only what needs changing.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a Change link during an amendment opens the question with the saved answers (repo-tests-p3-079, trace-e2e-p14-046).

requirements.statement: Continue on the amend review is held while any answer is invalid or incomplete (such as an arrival date outside 7 days back to 6 months ahead): the trader stays on the amend review and, as Design Release 2.1 draws it, no error summary or error message is shown. The draft review's error summary is not carried over to the amend review. Plants' amend review holds Continue the same way, in the same increment.
requirements.why: A resubmitted amendment must be complete and valid, and the hold itself meets that constraint; Design Release 2.1 draws the refused Continue as a silent hold and DR1 judged nothing about the amend review, so the prototype wins (c-201).
requirements.deltaNote: Today an amendment reaches the declaration only once every task row is fulfilled (repo-tests-p3-085).

requirements.statement: Continue on a valid amend review goes to the Declaration page; ticking the declaration and pressing Continue resubmits the amendment.
requirements.why: An amendment is resubmitted through the same declaration as a first submission.
requirements.deltaNote: Continue on the amending review already leads to the Declaration, and ticking it resubmits (repo-tests-p3-088, repo-tests-p3-091, trace-e2e-p14-056).

requirements.statement: Resubmitting an amendment shows the ordinary 'Import notification submitted' confirmation with the notification's existing reference and no wording about an amendment; the same record becomes Submitted again, read only, with the edited answers, the dashboard shows the amended answers, and it can be amended again.
requirements.why: An amendment replaces the submitted notification rather than creating a second one.
requirements.deltaNote: Resubmission already lands on the submitted confirmation and the notification is Submitted, read only and amendable again with the edited value (repo-tests-p3-092, trace-e2e-p14-057, trace-e2e-p14-059). The dashboard cards' empty 'Date submitted' (trace-e2e-p14-062) is the notification list's, which drops that fact (req-1075).

requirements.statement: The cancel-amendment confirmation page's title and level-1 heading are 'Are you sure you want to cancel this amendment?', with no caption, in every set that amends (live animals, germinal products and plants).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording for cancelling an amendment, carried onto the page by the 9 October afternoon ruling; on a page the heading is the level-1 heading, where the pop-up drew a level-2.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the cancel-amend page's title and level-1 heading are 'Cancel this amendment?' (repo-frontend-p3-080, trace-e2e-p14-035), in plants too (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-105).

requirements.statement: The cancel-amendment confirmation page shows no paragraph explaining that changes will be discarded and the submitted version restored, in every set that amends.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's cancel-amendment confirmation has no description line, and the 9 October afternoon ruling carries that onto the page.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page says 'Your changes since you started amending will be discarded and the submitted version restored.' (repo-frontend-p3-081, trace-e2e-p14-036), as plants' does (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-106).

requirements.statement: The cancel-amendment confirm button reads 'Yes, cancel amendment' and is a standard (not warning) primary button.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree on this button.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's cancel-amend page already has a standard 'Yes, cancel amendment' button (repo-frontend-p3-082, trace-animals-fit-p3-038).

requirements.statement: The cancel-amendment confirmation page's way back is a link-styled 'Go back' that returns to the notification's view (the amend review while amending; plants' check answers view) and leaves the amendment in progress, replacing the secondary button 'No, return to notification', in every set that amends.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording and pattern for not cancelling; as a page at today's route, it goes back where today's way back goes.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the way back is a secondary button-styled link 'No, return to notification' to the notification view (repo-frontend-p3-083, trace-e2e-p14-039), and the same in plants (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-109).

requirements.statement: 'Cancel amend' (in the Amend status bar and beside Continue on the amend review) and the card's 'Cancel amendment' go to the cancel-amendment confirmation page at today's route (/notifications/{id}/cancel-amend in each set), which carries only the confirmation's heading and buttons: no journey strip and no Back link.
requirements.why: The 9 October afternoon ruling keeps the cancel confirmation as a separate page at today's route carrying the pop-up's wording, so the page holds what the pop-up held.
requirements.deltaNote: Today 'Cancel amendment' is a link under the review heading and on the card, reaching a page at /notifications/{id}/cancel-amend with the Amending journey strip and a Back link to the notification view (repo-frontend-p3-078, repo-frontend-p3-138, trace-e2e-p14-034, trace-e2e-p14-037); plants has the same page, reached from the amending card's 'Cancel amendment' link and its read-only view, with a Back link (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-102, repo-plantsfrontend-p3-110, repo-plantsfrontend-p9-115).

requirements.statement: Confirming the cancellation discards every edit made during the amendment, restores the submitted content and fulfilments, returns the notification to SUBMITTED with its original submitted time, records one NotificationAmendmentCancelled event, and takes the trader to that notification's view page, read only and showing Submitted.
requirements.why: Cancelling must leave the notification exactly as it was submitted.
requirements.deltaNote: Cancel-amend already restores the snapshot and returns to the read-only Submitted view (repo-backend-p2-105, trace-e2e-p14-045, trace-animals-fit-p3-047), in plants too (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-112, repo-plantsfrontend-p3-118). The restored view's Back link, which today goes to the notification's hub (trace-animals-fit-p3-050, trace-e2e-p14-052), is the view header's, not this requirement's.

requirements.statement: After an amendment is cancelled, the view page shows no success banner; the redirect to it keeps ?cancelled=1 in its address, as today, in every set that amends.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 returns to the view page without a message; the 9 October ruling keeps ?cancelled=1, because the prototype never decides URL shapes.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the view opens at ?cancelled=1 with a 'Success' banner reading 'The amendment has been cancelled and the submitted version restored.' (trace-animals-fit-p3-044, trace-animals-fit-p3-045, repo-tests-p3-080): the address stays, the banner goes. Plants already redirects with ?cancelled=1 and its fit test finds the restored view showing Submitted (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-112, repo-plantsfrontend-p3-118).

requirements.statement: Opening or posting cancel amendment for a notification that is not being amended changes nothing and returns the trader to the set's own notification list with no message, in every set that amends.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 guards the route silently; the 9 October afternoon ruling sends every 'overall dashboard' destination, this one included, to the set's own list.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a Submitted notification is redirected to its view page (plants: its check answers view), and any other status to the set's list (repo-frontend-p3-079, repo-frontend-p3-087, repo-plantsfrontend-p3-104).

requirements.statement: When copy as new, cancel amendment or delete fails to save, the page the trader came from is shown again with HTTP 500 and the recoverable-error banner, in every set that has the action.
requirements.why: A real save can fail; the prototype cannot express that.
requirements.deltaNote: Each controller already re-renders with 500 and the recoverable-error banner (repo-frontend-p3-076, repo-frontend-p3-088, repo-frontend-p3-102).

requirements.statement: In the animals sets (live animals and germinal products), Copy as new goes straight, with no confirmation, to the new draft's overview hub titled 'Overview', which has no Back link and no banner announcing the copy.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree that copying is immediate and quiet.
requirements.deltaNote: Copy already redirects straight to the new notification's overview with no banner (trace-e2e-p3-073, trace-e2e-p3-077, trace-animals-fit-p2-075).

requirements.statement: A copy is a new notification saved at once as a Draft, with its own new reference (same GBN-AG prefix, fresh suffix); the source is unchanged, the copy is independent of it, every copy is distinct, and a NotificationCreated event (carrying the acting user's organisation id to resolve address-book parties) is recorded for the copy only.
requirements.why: Copying must never alter or merge with the notification it came from.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend copy endpoint already makes a new DRAFT with a new reference and leaves the source alone (repo-backend-p2-042, repo-backend-p2-044, trace-e2e-p14-074).

requirements.statement: A copy carries over the origin of the import: country of origin, whether a region of origin code is required, and the region of origin code with its suffix.
requirements.why: These describe the trade, not the shipment, so they usually repeat.
requirements.deltaNote: The copy mapper keeps them (repo-backend-p2-047) and the copy's origin page comes back prefilled (trace-animals-fit-p2-078).

requirements.statement: A copy carries over the internal reference number, in the notification record as well as on the page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 carries it over with the import details.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend copy mapper clears the internal reference in the notification record (repo-backend-p2-048), though the copy's origin page shows it from the copied fulfilments (trace-animals-fit-p2-078).

requirements.statement: A copy carries over what is being imported: the commodity (id, code and name), the commodity selections, the selected species and the notification type (worked out from the copied answers when missing).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 marks What are you importing? Complete on the copy.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend copy mapper keeps the commodity name and each complement's type but clears every complement's species list (repo-backend-p2-049, repo-backend-p2-050, repo-backend-p2-051).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over the number of animals, the number of packages or the net weight: the copy's commodity details show To do, its Animals total reads 0 and its Packages/boxes total shows no figure.
requirements.why: Counts are specific to each shipment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the copy's overview carries the totals (1 animal, 5 packages) and marks Commodity details Complete (trace-e2e-p3-075, trace-e2e-p13-109, trace-animals-fit-p2-077), though the copy mapper clears them in the record (repo-backend-p2-051).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over animal identifiers (ear tags, passports and the like): the copy's Identification details show To do.
requirements.why: Identifiers belong to the animals in one shipment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the copy's Identification details show Complete (trace-e2e-p13-109, trace-e2e-p3-075), though the copy mapper drops identifiers from the record (repo-backend-p2-052).

requirements.statement: A copy carries over the main reason for import and its follow-ups: internal market purpose, transhipment destination country, transit exit border control post, transit destination country, and the temporary admission exit date and port of exit.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 marks Main import reason Complete on the copy.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend copy mapper keeps the reason, purpose, destination country and port of exit but clears the exit date (repo-backend-p2-053, repo-backend-p2-059, repo-backend-p2-062).

requirements.statement: A copy carries over the additional animal details: what the animals are certified for, whether unweaned animals are included, and the storage temperature.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 marks Additional details Complete on the copy.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend copy mapper keeps certified-for but clears the unweaned animals answer (repo-backend-p2-054).

requirements.statement: When copying a live-animals notification, a certified-for value that is no longer an option is mapped to a current one: 'Breeding' and 'Breeding and/or production' become 'Further keeping', 'Slaughter' stays 'Slaughter', and any other value not offered becomes 'Further keeping'.
requirements.why: A copy must not carry an answer the trader can no longer choose.

requirements.statement: A copy carries over the roles and addresses (place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer and place of destination, each in full as stored), the CPH number and the permanent address details.
requirements.why: Trading partners usually repeat between shipments.
requirements.deltaNote: The copy mapper keeps every party, the CPH number and the whole fulfilments payload (repo-backend-p2-055, repo-backend-p2-058, repo-backend-p2-063).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over the arrival details (port of entry, arrival date, means of transport, transport identification and transport document reference): the copy's Arrival details show To do.
requirements.why: Arrival is specific to each shipment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the copy's Arrival details show Complete (trace-e2e-p3-075, trace-e2e-p13-109), though the copy mapper clears the transport block in the record (repo-backend-p2-060).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over the transit countries.
requirements.why: The route is specific to each shipment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the copy's Transit countries show Complete (trace-e2e-p3-075, trace-e2e-p13-109).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over the transporter: the copy's Transport details show To do.
requirements.why: The transporter is chosen per shipment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the copy's Transport details show Complete (trace-e2e-p3-075).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over the contact address: the copy's Contact address shows To do.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks for the contact address again on each notification.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the copy's Contact address shows Complete (trace-e2e-p3-075, trace-animals-fit-p2-077), though the copy mapper clears the consignment block in the record (repo-backend-p2-061).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over uploaded documents: the copy's Upload documents shows To do.
requirements.why: Documents are specific to each shipment.
requirements.deltaNote: Upload documents already shows To do on a copy (trace-e2e-p3-076).

requirements.statement: Copying a notification that is being amended copies its submitted version, not the edits in progress.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copies the saved notification; an unfinished amendment is not yet the notification.
requirements.deltaNote: Today copying an AMEND notification copies its current, edited content (repo-backend-p2-066).

requirements.statement: Copy as new for a notification the trader cannot reach (unknown reference, or a status that cannot be copied such as deleted) changes nothing and returns to the set's own notification list with no message.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 guards the route silently; the 9 October afternoon ruling sends its 'overall dashboard' to the set's own list.
requirements.deltaNote: Copy already returns an unknown notification to the set's list with no banner (repo-frontend-p3-073); the backend refuses unknown (404) and uncopyable (400) sources (repo-backend-p2-037, repo-backend-p2-038).

requirements.statement: Copy as new is checked against the version the trader was looking at: if the notification changed since, nothing is copied and the trader returns to where they started (the dashboard or the notification's view page) with the 'The notification has been updated' banner. A stale copy from the view page must land on the view page, not on a missing check-answers page.
requirements.why: A trader must never copy content different from what they saw; the prototype cannot express concurrent edits.
requirements.deltaNote: The token check and banner exist (repo-frontend-p3-074, repo-backend-p2-040), but a stale copy started from the view page redirects to /notifications/{id}/check-answers?staleAction=1, which no route serves (repo-frontend-p3-075-m1).

requirements.statement: A notification being amended can be deleted (from the amend review's Delete button) in every set that amends, and the backend's soft-delete API description says DRAFT, SUBMITTED and AMEND notifications can be deleted.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 offers Delete during an amendment, and the API must describe what it does.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend and both frontends already delete AMEND notifications (repo-backend-p3-034, repo-frontend-p3-091, repo-plantsfrontend-p3-085), but the API description says only DRAFT and SUBMITTED (repo-backend-p3-035) and no fit spec proves deleting an amending notification (repo-frontend-p3-135-m1, repo-plantsfrontend-p3-101).

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation page identifies the notification in a GOV.UK summary list with the rows 'Reference number', 'Commodity', 'Number' and 'Origin' (the country of origin), in every set (live animals, germinal products and plants).
requirements.why: The trader confirms they are deleting the right notification; the 9 October afternoon ruling gives plants the same layout in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the delete page has only a heading, one sentence and two buttons (repo-frontend-p3-092, repo-frontend-p3-093), in plants too (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-086, repo-plantsfrontend-p3-087).

requirements.statement: In the animals sets, the delete page's Commodity row lists each commodity's common name with its species' Latin names in brackets, comma-separated (for example 'Sheep (Ovis Aries), Goat (Capra Hircus)'); for other live mammals each species' common name is used.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's format for naming what was notified.

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, the delete page's Number row shows the notification's total number of animals.
requirements.why: Animals are counted by head. The 9 October ruling splits this requirement by set; the germinal set's packages count is its own requirement.

requirements.statement: A delete page summary row with no value from the notification falls back to what the set's notification list shows for it, and shows 'Not applicable' when that is empty too, in every set.
requirements.why: Every row shows something, even for an early draft.

requirements.statement: Below the summary the delete page says 'Confirm that you want to delete this notification.', in every set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's confirmation wording.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page has no such sentence (repo-frontend-p3-093).

requirements.statement: The delete page warns 'This action cannot be undone.', in every set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's warning wording.
requirements.deltaNote: Today it reads 'This cannot be undone.' (repo-frontend-p3-093, trace-e2e-p3-060), in plants too (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-087).

requirements.statement: The delete page's red warning button reads 'Yes, delete', in every set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's button wording.
requirements.deltaNote: Today it reads 'Yes, delete notification' (repo-frontend-p3-095, trace-animals-fit-p3-008), in plants too (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-088).

requirements.statement: Beside 'Yes, delete' the delete page has a plain link 'No, cancel' in the button group, replacing the secondary button 'No, return to dashboard', in every set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording and pattern for not deleting.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the way back is a secondary button-styled link 'No, return to dashboard' (repo-frontend-p3-096, trace-animals-fit-p3-009), in plants too (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-089).

requirements.statement: The delete page's Back link and 'No, cancel' both return to the notification's view page, in every set (plants' check answers view).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sends the trader back to the notification they were deleting.
requirements.deltaNote: Today both go to the set's list (repo-frontend-p3-097, trace-animals-fit-p3-010, trace-e2e-p3-063), in plants too (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-089, repo-plantsfrontend-p3-090).

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation page shows no journey strip (status tag and reference) above its heading, in every set; the summary list identifies the notification instead.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 builds the page from GOV.UK components only.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page shows the journey strip with the status tag and reference (repo-frontend-p3-094-m1, trace-e2e-p3-064).

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation page is titled 'Delete this notification? - Import notification service - GOV.UK' with the level-1 heading 'Delete this notification?', serves every deletable status, and can be opened directly by its address, in every set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree on the heading.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's delete page already has this title and heading for drafts and submitted notifications (trace-animals-fit-p3-006-m1, trace-animals-fit-p3-013), reached from each card's Delete (trace-animals-fit-p3-001), and plants' delete page has the same heading (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-086).

requirements.statement: Confirming the delete (a POST with the CSRF crumb) soft-deletes the notification: its status becomes DELETED and the record is kept; a repeat is a harmless no-op; a NotificationDeleted (draft) or NotificationSubmissionDeleted (submitted or amending) event is recorded with the actor and organisation id; an unknown reference gets 404. Plants soft-deletes through its own backend the same way.
requirements.why: The real store keeps deleted records for other services and audit; the prototype's outright removal cannot express persistence.
requirements.deltaNote: Delete already soft-deletes through the backend, idempotently, with the events (repo-backend-p3-033, repo-backend-p3-036, repo-backend-p3-040, trace-e2e-p14-078).

requirements.statement: After 'Yes, delete' the trader lands on the set's own notification list (the live-animals set root, the germinal products set root, plants' own list), and the redirect keeps ?deleted=1 in its address.
requirements.why: The 9 October afternoon ruling sends every Design Release 2.1 'overall dashboard' destination, the delete landing included, to the set's own list, replacing the INS landing; the 9 October ruling keeps ?deleted=1 on the redirect (c-198, c-269).
requirements.deltaNote: The live-animals delete already lands on /live-animals?deleted=1 (repo-frontend-p3-099, trace-e2e-p3-066), and plants' on its own list with deleted=1 (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-093); the germinal set gets it with its copy of the feature.

requirements.statement: The deletion success message reads 'Notification has been deleted' in every set (live animals, germinal products and plants): Design Release 2.1's wording for a page that does not know the deleted notification's reference, which the ?deleted=1 redirect does not carry.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording; its '<reference> has been deleted' form needs the reference on the list, and the 9 October ruling keeps the redirect's address as ?deleted=1.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the banner is titled 'Notification deleted' and reads 'The notification has been deleted.' (trace-animals-fit-p3-017, trace-animals-fit-p3-018, trace-e2e-p3-068). The banner's 'Success' title is req-1086's.

requirements.statement: A deleted notification no longer appears in the notification list, and searching for its reference finds nothing.
requirements.why: Deleted notifications are gone from the trader's view.
requirements.deltaNote: The deleted notification already disappears from the dashboard and its search (trace-animals-fit-p3-020, trace-e2e-p3-072).

requirements.statement: Opening or posting delete for a notification the trader cannot reach (unknown reference, another session's notification in plants, or a status that cannot be deleted) changes nothing and returns to the set's own notification list with no message, in every set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 guards the route; the real service must also check the record exists, which the prototype's POST does not; the 9 October afternoon ruling sends the guard to the set's own list.
requirements.deltaNote: Delete already refuses an unknown or non-deletable notification and returns to the set's list with no banner (repo-frontend-p3-100, repo-frontend-p3-101), as plants' does (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-085, repo-plantsfrontend-p3-093).

requirements.statement: The view page shows the notification's answers in the same six numbered sections and cards as the review page (1. About the consignment to 6. Contact address); the card contents follow the review page's requirements.
requirements.why: One rendering of a notification's answers serves review and view.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's notification view already renders the review page's six numbered sections (trace-animals-fit-p3-051); differences inside the cards are carried by the review page's requirements.

requirements.statement: The backend notification API supports the lifecycle: create gives DRAFT with a minted reference; save keeps DRAFT or AMEND; submit takes DRAFT or AMEND to SUBMITTED and stamps submittedAt; amend takes SUBMITTED to AMEND; cancel-amend takes AMEND back to SUBMITTED; copy reads DRAFT, SUBMITTED or AMEND and makes a new DRAFT; soft-delete makes DELETED. Each write advances the concurrency token, takes an optional actor, and callers from outside carry the API key.
requirements.why: Every action in this area rests on these transitions.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend already implements this lifecycle (repo-backend-p2-111), proven through the API (trace-e2e-p14-067, trace-e2e-p14-070, trace-e2e-p14-077).

requirements.statement: A notification is saved as a draft as the trader goes: one record per reference, keeping its created date, without errors or transient page state.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 autosaves drafts; the real service persists each save.
requirements.deltaNote: Each journey page's save already persists the whole record under its reference (repo-tests-p4-095, repo-tests-p4-096, trace-e2e-p14-083).

requirements.statement: The delete and cancel-amendment confirmations, the restored submitted view and a copied notification's overview have no serious or critical WCAG 2 A or AA axe violations, in the animals frontend and in plants.
requirements.why: The service must meet accessibility standards.
requirements.deltaNote: The fit specs already assert this (repo-frontend-p3-123, repo-frontend-p3-127, repo-frontend-p3-132).

requirements.statement: The tests repo's animals specs and page objects for amend, cancel amendment, copy as new and delete assert the Design Release 2.1 behaviour (new copy, dialogs, landing pages and banners) while still asserting ?cancelled=1 and ?deleted=1 on the cancel and delete redirects, keep the smoke-tagged cancel and delete cases, and cover what today goes unproven: deleting an amending notification and the guard redirects.
requirements.why: End-to-end proof must follow the changed behaviour.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's specs assert the current copy ('Yes, delete notification', 'Cancel this amendment?', 'Amending', ?deleted=1, ?cancelled=1) and do not prove a way back from delete (repo-tests-p3-095, repo-tests-p3-075, repo-tests-p3-099).

requirements.statement: Every new or changed string on the delete and cancel-amendment confirmations, the amend confirmation page and the view page has a Welsh entry, in the animals frontend and in plants.
requirements.why: Today's action pages carry Welsh copy, and the frontend's standing rule (req-1659) is that every new or changed piece of user-facing text has a Welsh version of the same shape; Design Release 2.1 is silent on Welsh, so nothing it shows overrides that rule.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the delete and cancel-amend pages have machine-drafted Welsh copy for their current strings (repo-frontend-p3-089, repo-frontend-p3-104), and plants' copies of them too (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-096, repo-plantsfrontend-p3-114).

requirements.statement: Delete and cancel amendment are checked against the version the trader opened, and the dashboard Amend carries a concurrency token.
requirements.why: Recorded for the report: delete and cancel-amend post a token nobody reads, and Amend posts none. Design Release 2.1 does not ask for a fix, so the programme does not make one.

requirements.statement: Soft delete checks that the caller owns the notification or is an admin.
requirements.why: Recorded for the report as an access-control weakness in the backend; Design Release 2.1 does not cover it, so it needs its own ticket.

requirements.statement: Create, save, copy, submit, amend and cancel-amend write audit records attributed to a user.
requirements.why: Recorded for the report: only deletes and replays are audited, and the write endpoints take no user id. Design Release 2.1 does not ask for audit.

requirements.statement: Backend edge cases answer with a client error rather than a server error: copy with a missing token or no content, amend with no fulfilments, a second submit or amend inside the outbox lock window, and submit of an empty notification.
