requirements.statement: Claims in this area's working set about pages next to the roles and addresses page and the pickers are built in their own areas, not here: the success banner and landing after adding an address, and the Edit details link on a copied party (party-address-add-and-edit); the CPH number page and the permanent address row's target (cph-permanent-and-contact); the review page's Roles and addresses and contact cards, their Edit details links and the 'Complete <section>' errors (review-and-submit); the page endings while amending or editing a template (journey-flow, templates); the redirect when a hidden section's page is opened (cph-permanent-and-contact); and plants' confirmation page copy (review-and-submit). The trace gaps they record (no trace of 'Cancel and return to hub' on a picker or the CPH page, no snapshot of two stub-mode pickers) need nothing built.
requirements.why: Recorded so every claim in this area is weighed: each describes another page's content or a gap in the evidence, and its own area's requirements carry what is built.

requirements.statement: While a trader is creating or changing a live animals or germinal products template, each party picker's 'Add a new address' round trip and each role's 'Edit details' page work as they do in a notification, on the same pages: the handshake identifies the template being worked on, saving or cancelling on the INS add page returns to that template's own picker or Consignment addresses page with the template's answer set as it would be for a notification, and an edit changes only the template's copy, never the address book record. Nothing returns the trader to a notification.
requirements.why: Template mode is another way of walking the same journey pages and captures the same data; it never copies or forks the pages, and later page changes carry into it without rework (ruling 2026-10-09 templates). Today's handshake and edit pages are built around a notification, so without this a trader adding an address while building a template would lose their place.
requirements.deltaNote: Today there is no template mode; the add link sends the notification id (repo-frontend-p9-134) and the return lands on that notification's picker (repo-frontend-p9-139, repo-frontend-p9-149). Which validation template mode relaxes is the templates area's to settle, not this row's. Animals only: template mode is not added to plants.

requirements.statement: The plants review page's contact card re-reads the contact from the organisation's address book by its id instead of showing the copy the contact page saved, so a record corrected since it was chosen shows its current details and a deleted one shows 'Not provided'.
requirements.why: Out of scope: this is a plants-only inconsistency with the copy semantics plants' own decision d-013 and the animals contact page keep (req-773, c-124). No Design Release 2.1 row changes this behaviour in animals, so there is nothing to mirror into plants (the 2026-10-09 afternoon ruling leaves plants alone where no row has a plants equivalent); it goes to the report for plants to fix.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p7-072-m1: the review re-reads the record by addressId rather than showing the saved copy.

requirements.statement: Fit tests for plants' check answers, declaration and confirmation that today's suite lacks: check answers for plants for planting and wood (consignor card, arrival status row, already-arrived labels), the plants and wood late rule, the outstanding-party errors, the amendment's cancel control and banner, the Delete button, a refused or failed submission, and an accessibility check on the three review tests that run none.
requirements.why: A gap in today's plants test suite, not a look-and-feel difference from Design Release 2.1. It goes to the report; each increment that changes one of these pages proves its own change with its own tests.

requirements.statement: Inspector-side live access to a submitted plants notification, and projecting plants' late notification indicator into the plants backend's notification record for the regulator side.
requirements.why: Plants' own decisions d-066 and d-007 park both as backend and regulator-tooling work outside the notifier frontend, and trade-imports-plants-backend is not one of the programme's repos; no source in this programme asks for them.

requirements.statement: On the live animals list, a submitted notification that still has items outstanding shows what is outstanding as plain text on its card under the reference: 'ITAHC is missing' when no uploaded document is an ITAHC or health certificate, otherwise 'Information is missing' when its animal identifiers are incomplete, taken from what the record stored at submit.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 tells the trader on the list what still needs doing on an action-required notification, and the 9 October afternoon ruling brings the outstanding items onto the reframed list (inc-147) and the 'Action required' card (inc-131) from the status the animals backend records.
requirements.deltaNote: Today no card shows an outstanding-items message; the list has no action-required status (repo-frontend-p3-046).

requirements.statement: A live animals template holds the transit countries as answered on the set's own transit countries page, shows them on the template page in a card whose Change link changes them, and seeds them into a notification started from it.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's template page offers a Change link for transit countries and its 'use template' seeds them, yet its template never saves them; the templates ruling says template mode captures the same data as a notification on the same pages, so the default holds them (c-318).

requirements.statement: In the animals sets, a 'Submitted action required' notification can be amended, copied and deleted as a Submitted one can: 'Amend this notification' and the amend confirmation start its amendment (the backend's amend takes it to AMEND with the same snapshots), cancelling that amendment restores it to 'Submitted action required' with its submitted answers, Copy as new copies it into a new draft, and Delete soft-deletes it with a NotificationSubmissionDeleted event. Resubmitting the amendment records the status the outstanding items give at that moment.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 offers Amend this notification, Copy as new and Delete on an action-required notification exactly as on a Submitted one, and its status follows from the outstanding items, so restoring the submitted answers restores it. The 9 October afternoon ruling adds the status beside the others without changing them, so every action that accepts SUBMITTED today must accept it too, or the trader is refused on the very notification that needs their action.
requirements.deltaNote: Today there is no action-required status, and the backend's amend takes only SUBMITTED (repo-backend-p2-093), cancel-amend always returns to SUBMITTED (repo-backend-p2-100), copy reads only DRAFT, SUBMITTED and AMEND (repo-backend-p2-038) and soft delete takes only DRAFT, SUBMITTED and AMEND (repo-backend-p3-034). Design Release 2.1 offers the actions (trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-012) but never traces amending one (trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-121). Plants has no action-required status (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-076).

requirements.statement: In the animals sets, a 'Completed' notification can be copied (Copy as new makes a new draft from it) and deleted (soft delete, with a NotificationSubmissionDeleted event), but not amended: its view offers no 'Amend this notification', and amend for it is refused by the guard in req-1487.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 offers Copy as new and Delete, and no Amend, on a Completed notification. The status arrives only once the authorities' outcomes reach the service, so the actions wait with it.
requirements.deltaNote: No Completed status exists today; copy and soft delete accept only DRAFT, SUBMITTED and AMEND (repo-backend-p2-038, repo-backend-p3-034). Design Release 2.1 does not trace copying or deleting a Completed notification (trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-104, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-119). Whether plants takes the status is decided when it unblocks (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-065).
requirements.blockedBy: The authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) must send post-submission outcomes, including completed, back to the notification record, as req-1082 waits on; no Completed status reaches the service today.

requirements.statement: Submitting a plants notification stays a synchronous save of the whole fulfilment snapshot through the plants records port, with no outbox, GBN-AG or other event publishing and no PIMS routing, and plants' confirmation makes no promise about where the notification has gone; this programme adds no publishing to plants.
requirements.why: The GBN-AG events and PIMS route this area records are the animals backend's; plants' own ledger parks publishing, and Design Release 2.1 changes no plants persistence.
requirements.deltaNote: Plants' ledger d-047 (repo-plantsfrontend-p9-088) already submits by a synchronous persist with no publishing.

requirements.statement: Publishing plants notifications (an outbox, GBN-AG or another event, PIMS routing) and a plants backend mapper that carries every SI matter instead of only the reference number are not built in this programme.
requirements.why: Plants' ledger parks publishing (d-047), and it needs trade-imports-plants-backend, which is not one of the programme's repos.

requirements.statement: The plants journey keeps supplying coded values and its created and submitted times for management information and asks no question for it; 'time taken per notification' reads as created to submitted.
requirements.why: Plants' own ledger (d-082) settles what the journey records for MI; Design Release 2.1 changes none of it.
requirements.deltaNote: Plants' ledger d-082 (repo-plantsfrontend-p9-150) already records it.

requirements.statement: Which items the service navigation holds, and in what order, is carried by req-965 (Dashboard, Templates, Address book, Manage account, Log out on every frontend, with Welsh labels), not by a second requirement here. This area keeps each item's destination and current-item rules (req-1674 to req-1677, req-1907, req-2084).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 adds Templates between Dashboard and Address book, and the templates ruling lets the item go ahead on every frontend, plants included. The dashboard-home area already carries that change, so writing it twice would build it twice.
requirements.deltaNote: Today every frontend offers four items, Dashboard, Address book, Manage account and Log out (repo-frontend-p1-008, repo-insfrontend-p4-006, repo-plantsfrontend-p1-006, trace-e2e-p1-035); req-965 adds Templates.

requirements.statement: The Alpha phase banner itself, its grey tag, its wording 'This is a new service. Help us improve it and give your feedback by email.' and its Welsh twin on every page of every frontend, is carried by req-956, not by a second requirement here. This area keeps only the feedback link's destination (req-1684).
requirements.why: The banner already matches Design Release 2.1 and DR1's built row on every frontend. The dashboard-home area already carries it, so it is recorded once.

requirements.statement: The plants set is mounted at /high-risk-plants, every plants link carries that prefix, and every plants page renders in the shared layout, loading the service stylesheet and script. A request belongs to the set whose mount is the longest prefix of its path, and its routes, guards and chrome resolve inside that set; /health, /auth/* and paths outside every mount belong to no set and take the set-free chrome. A set must be mounted at a path starting with '/'.
requirements.why: This is how the shared chrome finds each set's home link, current item and error chrome, which the germinal-products set relies on when it is mounted beside live-animals (req-1907). It already exists.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p1-086 to p1-088 give the mount and layout, p1-097 to p1-100 the set context, and p1-055 to p1-058 the routes under the mount.

requirements.statement: The plants set's own engine and test wiring is not shared page chrome and no layout or sign-in row changes it: its session values, entry guard, flow configuration, dropped party references, section-status rule, persistence services and start-up checks, its England and Great Britain wording held as copy, and its copy-convention and copy-parity tests.
requirements.why: These claims sit in this area's slice of the plants frontend but describe the journey engine, its data and its tests. The journey-flow, consignment-parties and plants rows weigh them where a row changes them.
